title.en: Volume 109 Treatises 84: Selection and Examinations 4, Zhi Ke Jian Zhuo

sentences.zh: 志八十四

translations.literal: Treatise 84
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 84

sentences.zh: 選舉四

translations.literal: Selection and Examinations 4
translations.idiomatic: Selection and Examinations 4

sentences.zh: 制科薦擢

translations.literal: Special Decree Examinations and Recommendations
translations.idiomatic: Special Decree Examinations and Recommendations

sentences.zh: 制科者，天子親詔以待異等之才。

translations.literal: As for special decree examinations, the Son of Heaven issued personal edicts to await talents of extraordinary grade.
translations.idiomatic: Special decree examinations were occasions on which the emperor personally proclaimed a search for candidates of exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋設科最多，視為優選。

translations.literal: The Tang and Song established the most such examinations and regarded them as superior selection.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang and Song held these examinations most often and treated them as a distinguished path to office.

sentences.zh: 清代科目取士，垂為定制。

translations.literal: In the Qing dynasty, the regular examination subjects for selecting scholars became established custom.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qing, recruitment through the regular civil-service examination subjects settled into fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 其特詔舉行者，曰博學鴻詞科、經濟特科、孝廉方正科。

translations.literal: Those conducted by special edict were called the Erudition and Eloquence examination, the Economic Special examination, and the Filial and Upright examination.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations specially proclaimed included the Erudition and Eloquence (Boxue Hongci) subject, the Economic Special subject, and the Filial Integrity and Upright Conduct subject.

sentences.zh: 若經學，若巡幸召試，雖未設科，可附見也。

translations.literal: As for classical learning and imperial tour summon-examinations, although no subjects were formally established, they may be appended here for reference.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations for classical learning and examinations summoned during imperial tours, though not formally instituted as subjects, are recorded here by way of supplement.

sentences.zh: 聖祖敦崇實學，康熙甲辰、丁未兩科，改試策論。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor earnestly revered practical learning; in the Jiachen and Dingwei cycles of Kangxi, the two examinations were changed to test policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kangxi, who prized solid scholarship, ordered that the Jiachen and Dingwei sessions under his reign test policy essays instead.

sentences.zh: 既廷臣以古學不可猝辦，請仍舊制。

translations.literal: Subsequently court ministers, on the grounds that ancient learning could not be hurriedly completed, requested to restore the former system.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the ministers argued that candidates could not be expected to master classical learning on short notice and asked to revert to the old format.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔曰：「自古一代之興，必有博學鴻儒，備顧問著作之選。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, an edict said: "Since ancient times, whenever a dynasty has risen, there have surely been erudite scholars of broad learning to fill the ranks of advisers and compilers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of his reign, the emperor issued an edict: "From antiquity, the rise of every dynasty has been attended by broadly learned scholars fit to serve as advisers and compilers.

sentences.zh: 我朝定鼎以來，崇儒重道，培養人才。

translations.literal: Since our dynasty established its rule, it has honored Confucian learning, valued the Way, and cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of our dynasty, we have honored Confucian learning, upheld moral principle, and nurtured talent.

sentences.zh: 四海之廣，豈無奇才碩彥、學問淵通、文藻瑰麗、追蹤前哲者？

translations.literal: Within the vastness of the four seas, could there be no extraordinary talents and eminent scholars, whose learning is profound, whose literary ornament is splendid, and who follow in the footsteps of former sages?
translations.idiomatic: Across the breadth of the realm, can there be no extraordinary talents—scholars of profound learning, splendid literary gifts, and attainments worthy of the great sages of old?

sentences.zh: 凡有學行兼優、文詞卓越之人，不論已仕、未仕，在京三品以上及科、道官，在外督、撫、布、按，各舉所知，朕親試錄用。

translations.literal: All persons of combined learning and conduct, and of outstanding literary expression, whether already in office or not, shall be recommended each by his knowledge: in the capital by officials of the third rank and above and by censorate and secretariat officers; in the provinces by governors-general, governors, and provincial judicial commissioners—each to recommend whom he knows, and I shall personally examine and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever combines solid learning with upright conduct and excels in literary composition, whether already in office or not, shall be nominated by those who know him: in the capital by officials of the third rank and above and by censorate and secretariat officers; in the provinces by governors-general, governors, and provincial judicial commissioners. I shall examine them personally and appoint the successful candidates.

sentences.zh: 其內、外各官，果有真知灼見，在內開送吏部，在外開報督、撫，代為題薦。」

translations.literal: If any inner or outer officials truly have penetrating insight, those within shall forward memorials to the Board of Civil Appointments; those without shall report to governors-general and governors to submit recommendations on their behalf."
translations.idiomatic: If any official at court or in the provinces has genuine insight into a candidate's merits, he may forward the name to the Board of Civil Appointments in the capital or report it to the governor-general or governor in the provinces for formal recommendation."

sentences.zh: 嗣膺薦人員至京，詔戶部月給廩餼。

translations.literal: Subsequently those who had received recommendation arrived in the capital; an edict ordered the Board of Revenue to grant monthly grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, as recommended candidates arrived in the capital, the emperor ordered the Board of Revenue to provide them with monthly grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，召試體仁閣。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, they were summoned for examination at the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the third month, they were summoned to examination in the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 凡百四十三人，賜燕，試賦一、詩一，帝親覽試卷，取一等彭孫遹、倪燦、張烈、汪霦、喬萊、王頊齡、李因篤、秦松齡、周清原、陳維崧、徐嘉炎、陸葇、馮勖、錢中諧、汪楫、袁佑、硃彝尊、湯斌、汪琬、邱象隨等二十人。

translations.literal: In all, one hundred forty-three persons were granted a banquet; they were tested on one fu and one shi poem. The emperor personally reviewed the examination papers and selected twenty persons of the first grade, including Peng Sunyu, Ni Can, Zhang Lie, Wang Ying, Qiao Lai, Wang Xuling, Li Yindu, Qin Songling, Zhou Qingyuan, Chen Weisong, Xu Jiayan, Lu Ren, Feng Xu, Qian Zhongxie, Wang Ji, Yuan You, Zhu Yizun, Tang Bin, Wang Wan, and Qiu Xiangsui.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred forty-three candidates in all were given a banquet and examined on one fu and one shi poem. The emperor personally read the papers and named twenty first-grade passes, including Peng Sunyu, Ni Can, Zhang Lie, Wang Ying, Qiao Lai, Wang Xuling, Li Yindu, Qin Songling, Zhou Qingyuan, Chen Weisong, Xu Jiayan, Lu Ren, Feng Xu, Qian Zhongxie, Wang Ji, Yuan You, Zhu Yizun, Tang Bin, Wang Wan, and Qiu Xiangsui.

sentences.zh: 二等李來泰、潘耒、沈珩、施閏章、米漢雯、黃與堅、李鎧、徐釚、沈筠、周慶曾、尤侗、范必英、崔如岳、張鴻烈、方象瑛、李澄中、吳元龍、龐塏、毛奇齡、錢金甫、吳任臣、陳鴻績、曹宜溥、毛升芳、曹禾、黎騫、高詠、龍燮、邵吳遠、嚴繩孫等三十人。

translations.literal: Of the second grade were thirty persons, including Li Laitai, Pan Lei, Shen Heng, Shi Runzhang, Mi Hanwen, Huang Yujian, Li Kai, Xu Qian, Shen Yun, Zhou Qingzeng, You Tong, Fan Biying, Cui Ruyue, Zhang Honglie, Fang Xiangying, Li Chengzhong, Wu Yuanlong, Pang Kai, Mao Qiling, Qian Jinfu, Wu Renchen, Chen Hongji, Cao Yipu, Mao Shengfang, Cao He, Li Qian, Gao Yong, Long Xie, Shao Wuyuan, and Yan Shengsun.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty candidates received second grade, among them Li Laitai, Pan Lei, Shen Heng, Shi Runzhang, Mi Hanwen, Huang Yujian, Li Kai, Xu Qian, Shen Yun, Zhou Qingzeng, You Tong, Fan Biying, Cui Ruyue, Zhang Honglie, Fang Xiangying, Li Chengzhong, Wu Yuanlong, Pang Kai, Mao Qiling, Qian Jinfu, Wu Renchen, Chen Hongji, Cao Yipu, Mao Shengfang, Cao He, Li Qian, Gao Yong, Long Xie, Shao Wuyuan, and Yan Shengsun.

sentences.zh: 三、四等俱報罷。

translations.literal: Those of the third and fourth grades were all reported dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates in the third and fourth grades were all dismissed without appointment.

sentences.zh: 命閣臣取前代制科舊事，查議授職。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Grand Secretariat ministers to gather precedents of former dynasties' special decree examinations and deliberate on conferring offices.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Grand Secretariat ministers to consult precedents from earlier dynasties' special decree examinations and recommend appropriate appointments.

sentences.zh: 尋議：「兩漢授無常職。

translations.literal: Soon they deliberated: "In the two Han dynasties appointments had no fixed offices.
translations.idiomatic: They soon reported: "Under the two Han dynasties, appointments carried no fixed offices.

sentences.zh: 晉上第授尚書郎。

translations.literal: In Jin, those of the highest grade were appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, top-ranked candidates were made Gentlemen of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 唐制策高等特授尊官，次等予出身，因有及第、出身之目。

translations.literal: In Tang, those of high grade in the policy-examination were specially granted exalted offices; those of lower grade were given qualification status, hence the categories of 'passed' and 'qualified.'
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, high scorers on the policy examination received exceptional appointments to high office, while lower scorers received qualification status—hence the distinctions of jidi ('passed') and chushen ('qualified').

sentences.zh: 宋分五等：一、二等皆不次擢用；

translations.literal: Song divided into five grades: the first and second grades were all promoted out of turn;
translations.idiomatic: Song divided results into five grades: first- and second-grade candidates were all promoted ahead of the usual order;

sentences.zh: 三等為上等，恩數視廷試第一人；

translations.literal: the third grade counted as upper, with favors equal to the first place in the palace examination;
translations.idiomatic: third grade counted as upper rank, with privileges equal to the top palace examination graduate;

sentences.zh: 四等為中等，視廷試第三人；

translations.literal: the fourth grade counted as middle, equal to the third place in the palace examination;
translations.idiomatic: fourth grade as middle rank, equal to the third-place palace examination graduate;

sentences.zh: 皆賜制科出身。

translations.literal: all were granted special-decree-examination qualification.
translations.idiomatic: all received the qualification status of special decree examination graduates.

sentences.zh: 五等為下等，賜進士出身。」

translations.literal: the fifth grade counted as lower, granted jinshi qualification."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth grade counted as lower rank and received jinshi qualification status."

sentences.zh: 得旨，俱授為翰林官。

translations.literal: Receiving the imperial rescript, all were appointed as Hanlin officials.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving the imperial approval, all successful candidates were appointed to Hanlin posts.

sentences.zh: 以光祿少卿邵吳遠為侍讀。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Shao Wuyuan was made Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Wuyuan, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, was appointed Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 道員、郎中湯斌等四人為侍講。

translations.literal: The circuit intendant and director Tang Bin and three others were made Lecturers-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin, a circuit intendant and former director, and three others were appointed Lecturers-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 進士出身之主事，中、行、評、博，內閣典籍，知縣及未仕之進士彭孫遹等十八人為編修。

translations.literal: Eighteen persons, including jinshi-qualified secretaries, secretaries in the central, personnel, censorial, and tribute bureaus, Grand Secretariat archivists, magistrates, and unappointed jinshi such as Peng Sunyu, were made compilers.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen men—including jinshi secretaries, bureau secretaries, Grand Secretariat archivists, magistrates, and unappointed jinshi such as Peng Sunyu—were made Hanlin compilers.

sentences.zh: 舉、貢出身之推、知，教職，革職之檢討、知縣及未仕之舉、貢、廕、監、布衣倪燦等二十七人為檢討。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven persons, including provincial administrators and magistrates of juren and tribute-student origin, educational officials, dismissed compilers and magistrates, and unappointed juren, tribute students, yin-qualified candidates, students of the Imperial Academy, and commoners such as Ni Can, were made revisers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven others—including provincial administrators and magistrates drawn from juren and tribute-student ranks, educational officials, dismissed revisers and magistrates, and unappointed juren, tribute students, yin candidates, academy students, and commoners such as Ni Can—were made Hanlin revisers.

sentences.zh: 俱入史館，纂修明史。

translations.literal: All entered the Historiography Institute to compile the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: All were assigned to the Historiography Institute to compile the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 時富平李因篤、長洲馮勖、秀水硃彝尊、吳江潘耒、無錫嚴繩孫，皆以布衣入選，海內榮之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yindu of Fuping, Feng Xu of Changzhou, Zhu Yizun of Xiushui, Pan Lei of Wujiang, and Yan Shengsun of Wuxi all entered selection as commoners in plain dress, and the realm honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Yindu of Fuping, Feng Xu of Changzhou, Zhu Yizun of Xiushui, Pan Lei of Wujiang, and Yan Shengsun of Wuxi were all selected though they held no official rank—a distinction celebrated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 其年老未與試之杜越、傅山、王方穀等，文學素著，俱授內閣中書，許回籍。

translations.literal: Those advanced in years who had not taken the examination, such as Du Yue, Fu Shan, and Wang Fanggu, were all of long-standing literary renown and were appointed Grand Secretariat secretaries, permitted to return to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yue, Fu Shan, Wang Fanggu, and others who were too old to sit the examination but were already renowned for their scholarship were all appointed Grand Secretariat secretaries and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，詔曰：「博學鴻詞之科，所以待卓越淹通之士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, an edict said: "The Erudition and Eloquence subject exists to await outstanding and broadly accomplished scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, an edict declared: "The Erudition and Eloquence examination exists to reward scholars of exceptional breadth and depth.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，特詔薦舉，召試授職，得人極盛。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, a special edict summoned recommendations; those summoned for examination received offices, and the harvest of talent was extremely abundant.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi's seventeenth year a special edict called for recommendations, and those examined and appointed produced an exceptionally rich harvest of talent.

sentences.zh: 數十年來，未嘗廣為搜羅。

translations.literal: For several decades, there had been no broad search.
translations.idiomatic: For decades no comparable broad search had been undertaken.

sentences.zh: 朕延攬維殷，宜有枕經葄史、殫見洽聞、足稱鴻博之選者，當特修曠典，嘉予旁求。

translations.literal: I am eager in recruitment; there ought to be those who pillow themselves on the classics and coverlets of history, whose exhaustive knowledge and comprehensive hearing suffice to be called erudite and eloquent selections—therefore I shall specially restore this grand precedent and commend my wide search.
translations.idiomatic: I am eager to recruit talent. There must be scholars steeped in the classics and histories, of exhaustive learning and wide knowledge, worthy of the title 'erudite and eloquent.' I shall therefore restore this grand precedent and commend my search far and wide.

sentences.zh: 在京滿、漢三品以上，在外督、撫、學政，悉心體訪，保題送部。

translations.literal: In the capital, Manchu and Han officials of the third rank and above; in the provinces, governors-general, governors, and education commissioners shall diligently investigate and recommend, submitting nominations to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, Manchu and Han officials of the third rank and above; in the provinces, governors-general, governors, and education commissioners shall investigate carefully and submit nominations to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 朕臨軒親試，優加錄用。」

translations.literal: I shall personally examine them at the imperial audience hall and favorably appoint the successful."
translations.idiomatic: I shall examine them personally at court and appoint the successful candidates with special favor."

sentences.zh: 詔書初下，中外大吏，以事關曠典，相顧遲回。

translations.literal: When the edict was first issued, great officials within and without, because the matter concerned a grand precedent, looked at one another and hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict first appeared, senior officials at court and in the provinces, mindful that the matter involved a grand and rare precedent, hesitated and held back.

sentences.zh: 逾年，僅河東督臣舉一人，直隸督臣舉二人，他省未有應者。

translations.literal: After more than a year, only the governor-general of Hedong recommended one person, the governor-general of Zhili recommended two, and other provinces had no respondents.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year passed with only the governor-general of Hedong recommending one candidate, the governor-general of Zhili two, and no responses from other provinces.

sentences.zh: 詔責諸臣觀望。

translations.literal: An edict reproached the ministers for waiting and watching.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked the officials for their hesitation.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，再詔督促。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he again issued an edict urging them on.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qianlong ascended the throne, he issued another edict pressing for compliance.

sentences.zh: 期以一年內齊集闕下，先至者月給廩餼。

translations.literal: They were required to assemble at the capital within one year; those arriving first received monthly grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates were to gather at the capital within one year; those who arrived early received monthly grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，御史吳元安言：「薦舉博學鴻詞，原期得湛深經術、敦崇實學之儒，詩賦雖取兼長，經史尤為根柢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, the censor Wu Yuan'an said: "In recommending candidates for Erudition and Eloquence, the original expectation was to obtain Confucians of profound classical learning and earnest practical scholarship; although fu and shi poetry may be required as combined strengths, the classics and histories are especially the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's first year, Censor Wu Yuan'an argued: "Recommendations for Erudition and Eloquence were meant to produce scholars of deep classical learning and solid practical scholarship. Poetry may be tested as a secondary skill, but the classics and histories are the true foundation.

sentences.zh: 若徒駢綴儷偶，推敲聲律，縱有文藻可觀，終覺名實未稱。」

translations.literal: If one merely strings together parallel couplets and polishes tonal rules, even if the literary ornament is admirable, in the end name and reality do not match."
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who merely string together parallel couplets and polish tonal patterns may write pleasing prose, yet in the end their reputation will not match their substance."

sentences.zh: 下吏部議，定為兩場，賦、詩外增試論、策。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Board of Civil Appointments for deliberation; it was fixed as two sessions, with policy essays and memorials added beyond fu and shi poetry.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Civil Appointments was ordered to deliberate and fixed the format at two sessions, adding policy essays and memorials to the fu and shi requirements.

sentences.zh: 九月，召試百七十六人於保和殿，賜燕如例。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, one hundred seventy-six persons were summoned for examination at the Hall of Preserving Harmony and granted a banquet according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, one hundred seventy-six candidates were examined in the Hall of Preserving Harmony and given the customary banquet.

sentences.zh: 試題首場賦、詩、論各一，二場制策二。

translations.literal: The examination topics: in the first session one fu, one shi, and one essay each; in the second session two policy memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The first session required one fu, one shi, and one essay; the second session required two policy memorials.

sentences.zh: 取一等五人，劉綸、潘安禮、諸錦、于振、杭世駿等，授編修。

translations.literal: Five persons of the first grade were selected, including Liu Lun, Pan Anli, Zhu Jin, Yu Zhen, and Hang Shijun, and appointed compilers.
translations.idiomatic: Five first-grade candidates—Liu Lun, Pan Anli, Zhu Jin, Yu Zhen, and Hang Shijun—were appointed Hanlin compilers.

sentences.zh: 二等十人，陳兆侖、劉藻、夏之蓉、周長發、程恂等，授檢討；

translations.literal: Ten persons of the second grade, including Chen Zhaolun, Liu Zao, Xia Zhirong, Zhou Changfa, and Cheng Xun, were appointed revisers;
translations.idiomatic: Ten second-grade candidates—including Chen Zhaolun, Liu Zao, Xia Zhirong, Zhou Changfa, and Cheng Xun—were made revisers;

sentences.zh: 楊度汪、沈廷芳、汪士鍠、陳士璠、齊召南等，授庶吉士。

translations.literal: Yang Duwang, Shen Tingfang, Wang Shihong, Chen Shifan, Qi Zhaonan, and others were appointed Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Duwang, Shen Tingfang, Wang Shihong, Chen Shifan, Qi Zhaonan, and others were made Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 二年，補試體仁閣，首場制策二，二場賦、詩、論各一。

translations.literal: In the second year, a supplementary examination was held at the Hall of Embodied Benevolence: the first session had two policy memorials; the second session had one fu, one shi, and one essay each.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a supplementary examination was held in the Hall of Embodied Benevolence: the first session required two policy memorials; the second required one fu, one shi, and one essay.

sentences.zh: 取一等萬松齡，授檢討。

translations.literal: Wan Songling of the first grade was selected and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Songling, the sole first-grade pass, was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 二等張漢，授檢討；

translations.literal: Zhang Han of the second grade was appointed reviser;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han of the second grade was made reviser;

sentences.zh: 硃荃、洪世澤，授庶吉士。

translations.literal: Zhu Quan and Hong Shize were appointed Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quan and Hong Shize were made Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 自康、乾兩朝，再舉詞科，與其選者，山林隱逸之數，多於縉紳，右文之盛，前古罕聞。

translations.literal: From the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, when the literary subject was held twice, among those selected the number of recluses in mountains and forests exceeded that of girdled officials; the splendor of honoring literature was rarely heard of in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, when the literary examination was held twice, recluses and private scholars outnumbered serving officials among the successful candidates—a degree of literary patronage rarely matched in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 時承平累葉，海內士夫多致力根柢之學，天子又振拔淹滯，以示風勵，爰有保薦經學之制。

translations.literal: At that time, after generations of sustained peace, scholars throughout the realm largely devoted themselves to foundational learning; the Son of Heaven also raised up the long-stagnant to display encouragement by example, whereupon there was the institution of recommending classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: In an era of prolonged peace, scholars across the empire devoted themselves to foundational learning, while the emperor lifted long-neglected talent to set an example—hence the institution for recommending experts in classical learning.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，詔曰：「崇尚經術，有關世道人心。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, an edict said: "Honoring classical learning bears upon the ways of the age and the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's fourteenth year, an edict declared: "Honoring classical learning bears directly on the moral order of society and the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 今海宇昇平，學士大夫精研本業，窮年矻矻，宗仰儒先者，當不乏人。

translations.literal: Now within the seas all is ascendant peace; scholar-officials diligently study their proper occupations, toiling year after year—those who revere and follow the former Confucians should not be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm enjoys peace, scholar-officials who devote themselves year after year to their proper studies and revere the sages of old should not be hard to find.

sentences.zh: 大學士、九卿、督、撫，其公舉所知，不限進士、舉人、諸生及退休、閒廢人員，能潛心經學者，慎選毋濫。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries, the Nine Ministers, governors-general, and governors shall jointly recommend those they know, not limited to jinshi, juren, licentiates, or retired and idle personnel—those able to devote themselves quietly to classical learning; choose carefully and do not be indiscriminate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries, the Nine Ministers, governors-general, and governors shall jointly nominate candidates they know, without restriction to jinshi, juren, licentiates, or retired and idle scholars—provided they are devoted to classical learning. Choose carefully and do not recommend indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 尋中外疏薦者四十餘人。

translations.literal: Soon more than forty persons were recommended in memorials from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Soon more than forty candidates were recommended in memorials from court and provinces alike.

sentences.zh: 帝為防幸進，下廷臣覆覈，得陳祖范、吳鼎、梁錫興、顧棟高四人。

translations.literal: The emperor, to guard against favor-seekers, sent the matter down to court ministers for re-examination and obtained four persons: Chen Zufan, Wu Ding, Liang Xixing, and Gu Donggao.
translations.idiomatic: To guard against favor-seekers, the emperor ordered a court review and confirmed four candidates: Chen Zufan, Wu Ding, Liang Xixing, and Gu Donggao.

sentences.zh: 命呈覽著述，派翰林、中書官在武英殿各繕一部。

translations.literal: He ordered their writings presented for inspection and dispatched Hanlin and secretariat officials to copy one set each in the Hall of Martial Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered their writings submitted for review and assigned Hanlin and secretariat officials to copy one complete set of each in the Hall of Martial Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 尋授鼎、錫興國子監司業，召對勤政殿。

translations.literal: Soon Ding and Xixing were appointed vice directors of the Directorate of Education; they were summoned for audience at the Hall of Diligent Government.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ding and Liang Xixing were soon appointed vice directors of the Directorate of Education and summoned to audience in the Hall of Diligent Government.

sentences.zh: 祖范、棟高以年老不能供職，俱授司業銜。

translations.literal: Zufan and Donggao, because of advanced age, could not serve in office and were both granted the title of vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zufan and Gu Donggao, being too old to take up office, were both granted the honorary title of vice director.

sentences.zh: 後不復舉行。

translations.literal: Afterward it was not held again.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was not revived afterward.

sentences.zh: 至屬車臨幸，宏獎士林，康熙四十二年、四十四年，聖祖巡幸江、浙，召試士子，中選者賜白金，赴京錄用有差。

translations.literal: As for the imperial entourage on tour, broadly rewarding the scholarly community—in the forty-second and forty-fourth years of Kangxi, the Sacred Ancestor toured Jiangsu and Zhejiang, summoned scholars for examination, and those selected were granted white silver; going to the capital for appointment differed in degree.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled in person, he generously rewarded the scholarly community. In the forty-second and forty-fourth years of Kangxi, the emperor toured Jiangsu and Zhejiang, examined local scholars, and granted silver to successful candidates; those who proceeded to the capital received appointments of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 高宗六幸江、浙，三幸山東，四幸天津，凡士子進獻詩賦者，召試行在。

translations.literal: Gaozong toured Jiangsu and Zhejiang six times, Shandong three times, and Tianjin four times; all scholars who presented fu and shi poetry were summoned for examination at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianlong toured Jiangsu and Zhejiang six times, Shandong three times, and Tianjin four times; scholars who submitted poetry were examined at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 優等予出身，授內閣中書；

translations.literal: Those of superior grade were granted qualification status and appointed Grand Secretariat secretaries;
translations.idiomatic: Top candidates received qualification status and were appointed Grand Secretariat secretaries;

sentences.zh: 次者賜束帛。

translations.literal: those of lower grade were granted bundles of silk.
translations.idiomatic: lower-ranked candidates received bundles of silk.

sentences.zh: 仁宗東巡津、淀，西幸五台，召試之典，亦如前例。

translations.literal: Renzong toured east to Tianjin and the Baiyangdian marshes and west to Wutai; the precedent of summon-examination followed the former cases.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiaqing toured east to Tianjin and the Baiyangdian region and west to Wutai Mountain; the summon-examination followed the same precedent.

sentences.zh: 道光以後，科舉偏重時文。

translations.literal: After Daoguang, the civil examinations emphasized contemporary-style essays.
translations.idiomatic: After the Daoguang reign, the civil examinations came to emphasize contemporary-style essays.

sentences.zh: 沿習既久，庸濫浮偽，浸失精意。

translations.literal: As the practice continued long, mediocrity, indiscriminateness, superficiality, and falsity gradually lost the refined intent.
translations.idiomatic: Long custom bred mediocrity, empty display, and insincerity, and the original purpose was gradually lost.

sentences.zh: 三十年，候補京堂張錫庚請復開博學鴻詞科，以儲人才。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the expectant capital official Zhang Xigeng requested reopening the Erudition and Eloquence subject to store up talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, expectant capital official Zhang Xigeng petitioned to reopen the Erudition and Eloquence examination to build up the talent pool.

sentences.zh: 禮部議以非當務之急，遂止。

translations.literal: The Board of Rites deliberated that it was not an urgent task of the moment and thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites ruled that it was not an urgent priority, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 洎光緒中葉，外侮孔棘，海內皇皇，昌言變法。

translations.literal: By the middle of Guangxu, foreign aggression was extremely pressing; within the seas all were anxious, and reform was openly advocated.
translations.idiomatic: By the mid-Guangxu period, foreign aggression had become acute, anxiety spread throughout the country, and calls for reform grew loud.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，貴州學政嚴修請設經濟特科，下總理各國事務衙門會禮部覈議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Guizhou education commissioner Yan Xiu requested establishing the Economic Special subject; the matter was sent down to the Office for Managing Affairs of All Nations to deliberate jointly with the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Guizhou Education Commissioner Yan Xiu petitioned to establish the Economic Special examination; the matter was referred to the Zongli Yamen for joint deliberation with the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八月，慈禧皇太后臨朝訓政，以經濟特科易滋流弊，罷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Empress Dowager Cixi assumed regency at court and, on the grounds that the Economic Special subject easily bred abuses, abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Empress Dowager Cixi resumed regency and abolished the Economic Special examination on the grounds that it would invite abuse.

sentences.zh: 庚子，京師構亂，乘輿播遷。

translations.literal: In the Gengzi year, the capital was thrown into disorder and the imperial carriage was moved in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the capital was thrown into turmoil and the court fled.

sentences.zh: 兩宮怵於時局阽危，亟思破格求才，以資治理。

translations.literal: The two palaces were alarmed at the imminent peril of the times and urgently thought to seek talent outside regular rules to supply governance.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by the imminent crisis, the two palaces urgently sought to recruit talent by exceptional means to strengthen governance.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，皇太后詔舉經濟特科，命各部、院堂官及各省督、撫、學政保薦，有志慮忠純、規模閎遠、學問淹通、洞達中外時務者，悉心延攬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the empress dowager issued an edict to hold the Economic Special subject, ordering department and bureau chiefs and provincial governors-general, governors, and education commissioners to recommend those of loyal intent and pure resolve, broad scope and far-reaching plan, profound and comprehensive learning, and penetrating understanding of Chinese and foreign affairs of the time—diligently to recruit them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the empress dowager proclaimed the Economic Special examination and ordered ministry chiefs and provincial governors and education commissioners to recommend men of loyal character, broad vision, profound learning, and penetrating grasp of domestic and foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 並下政務大臣擬定考試事宜。

translations.literal: The matter was also sent down to administrative affairs grand ministers to draft examination arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers of state affairs were also ordered to draft the examination regulations.

sentences.zh: 御史陳秉崧奏請力除夤緣積習，詔飭諸臣務矢至公。

translations.literal: The censor Chen Bingsong memorialized requesting strenuous removal of the accumulated habit of currying favor; an edict admonished all ministers to be utterly impartial.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Bingsong memorialized urging the eradication of patronage networks; an edict admonished all officials to act with absolute impartiality.

sentences.zh: 既三品以下京卿紛紛保送，帝覺其冗濫，適太僕少卿隆恩薦疏，上竟報寢，並命撤銷太常少卿李擢英前保諸人。

translations.literal: When capital officials below the third rank all rushed to submit recommendations, the emperor felt it redundant and indiscriminate; just then the Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Long En's recommendation memorial arrived, and the throne ultimately reported it shelved, also ordering revocation of those formerly recommended by the Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Zhuoying.
translations.idiomatic: As capital officials below the third rank flooded the court with nominations, the emperor found the list excessive. When a recommendation from Vice Minister Long En of the Court of the Imperial Stud arrived, the throne shelved it and ordered the withdrawal of candidates previously nominated by Vice Minister Li Zhuoying of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，政務處議定考試之制，如廷試例，於保和殿天子親策之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Bureau of Government Affairs deliberated and fixed the examination system, following the palace examination precedent, with the Son of Heaven personally setting questions at the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the Bureau of Government Affairs finalized the examination format on the model of the palace examination, with the emperor setting the questions personally in the Hall of Preserving Harmony.

sentences.zh: 凡試二日，首場入選者，始許應覆試，均試論一、策一。

translations.literal: The examination lasted two days in all; only those who passed the first session were permitted to take the second; all were tested on one essay and one policy memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The examination lasted two days; only first-session passes were admitted to the second, and both sessions required one essay and one policy memorial.

sentences.zh: 簡大臣考校，取一等袁家穀、張一麟、方履中、陶炯照、徐沅、胡玉縉、秦錫鎮、俞陛雲、袁勵准等九人，二等馮善徵、羅良鑒、秦樹聲、魏家驊、吳鍾善、錢鑅、蕭應椿、梁煥奎、蔡寶善、張孝謙、端緒、麥鴻鈞、許岳鍾、張通謨、楊道霖、張祖廉、吳烈、陳曾壽等十八人。

translations.literal: Grand ministers were selected to examine and grade; nine persons of the first grade were taken, including Yuan Jiagu, Zhang Yilin, Fang Lüzhong, Tao Jiongzhao, Xu Yuan, Hu Yujin, Qin Xizhen, Yu Biyun, and Yuan Lizhun; eighteen of the second grade, including Feng Shanzheng, Luo Liangjian, Qin Shusheng, Wei Jiahua, Wu Zhongshan, Qian Hong, Xiao Yingchun, Liang Huankui, Cai Baoshan, Zhang Xiaoqian, Duan Xu, Mai Hongjun, Xu Yuezhong, Zhang Tongmo, Yang Daolin, Zhang Zulian, Wu Lie, and Chen Zengshou.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers were appointed examiners. Nine candidates received first grade, including Yuan Jiagu, Zhang Yilin, Fang Lüzhong, Tao Jiongzhao, Xu Yuan, Hu Yujin, Qin Xizhen, Yu Biyun, and Yuan Lizhun; eighteen received second grade, including Feng Shanzheng, Luo Liangjian, Qin Shusheng, Wei Jiahua, Wu Zhongshan, Qian Hong, Xiao Yingchun, Liang Huankui, Cai Baoshan, Zhang Xiaoqian, Duan Xu, Mai Hongjun, Xu Yuezhong, Zhang Tongmo, Yang Daolin, Zhang Zulian, Wu Lie, and Chen Zengshou.

sentences.zh: 迨授官命下，京職、外任，僅就原階略予升敘，舉、貢用知縣、州佐，以視康、乾時詞科恩遇，浸不如矣。

translations.literal: When appointment orders were issued, capital and provincial offices merely received slight promotion in rank from their original grades; juren and tribute students were used as magistrates and prefectural assistants—compared with the favors of the literary subject in the Kangxi and Qianlong periods, they gradually fell short.
translations.idiomatic: When appointments were issued, capital and provincial officials received only modest promotions from their existing ranks, and juren and tribute students were assigned as magistrates or prefectural assistants—rewards far less generous than those granted to literary examination graduates under Kangxi and Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，御史俾壽請特開制科，政務處大臣議以「孝廉方正、直言極諫兩科，皆無實際，惟博學鴻詞科，康熙、乾隆間兩次舉行，得人稱盛。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, the censor Bi Shou requested specially opening the special decree subject; grand ministers of the Bureau of Government Affairs deliberated that "the two subjects of Filial Integrity and Upright Conduct and Blunt Remonstrance to the Utmost both have no practical substance; only the Erudition and Eloquence subject, held twice in the Kangxi and Qianlong periods, gained men praised as flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, Censor Bi Shou petitioned to reopen the special decree examination. Grand ministers of the Bureau of Government Affairs argued that "the Filial Integrity and Blunt Remonstrance subjects serve little practical purpose, whereas the Erudition and Eloquence examination, held twice under Kangxi and Qianlong, produced a celebrated harvest of talent.

sentences.zh: 際茲文學漸微，保存國粹，實為今日急務。

translations.literal: At this juncture, as literature gradually declines, preserving the national essence is truly today's urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: At a time when literary culture is in decline, preserving the national cultural heritage is an urgent task of the day.

sentences.zh: 應下學部籌議」。

translations.literal: It should be sent down to the Ministry of Education for planning and deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: The matter should be referred to the Ministry of Education for planning."

sentences.zh: 時方詔各省徵召耆儒碩彥。

translations.literal: At that time an edict was just being issued to the provinces to summon venerable Confucians and eminent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was issuing edicts to the provinces summoning venerable scholars.

sentences.zh: 湖南舉人王闓運被薦，授翰林檢討。

translations.literal: The Hunan juren Wang Kaiyun was recommended and appointed Hanlin reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kaiyun, a juren from Hunan, was recommended and appointed Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 兩江、安徽相繼薦舉王耕心、孫葆田、程朝儀、吳傳綺、姚永朴、姚永概、馮澂等。

translations.literal: Liangjiang and Anhui successively recommended Wang Gengxin, Sun Baotian, Cheng Chaoyi, Wu Chuanqi, Yao Yongpu, Yao Yonggai, Feng Cheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangjiang and Anhui authorities successively recommended Wang Gengxin, Sun Baotian, Cheng Chaoyi, Wu Chuanqi, Yao Yongpu, Yao Yonggai, Feng Cheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 部議以諸人覃研經史，合於詞科之選，俟章程議定，陳請舉行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that these persons had deeply studied the classics and histories and suited selection for the literary subject; they would await deliberation and fixing of regulations, then memorialize requesting implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that these scholars, having devoted themselves to the classics and histories, were fit candidates for the literary examination and would be presented for implementation once the regulations were finalized.

sentences.zh: 未幾，德宗崩，遂寢。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Dezong passed away, and the matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Guangxu died, and the examination was shelved.

sentences.zh: 孝廉方正科，始於康熙六十一年，世宗登極，詔直省府、州、縣、衛各舉孝廉方正，賜六品章服，備召用。

translations.literal: The Xiaolian Fangzheng examination began in the sixty-first year of Kangxi. When the Shizong emperor ascended the throne, he issued an edict ordering each prefecture, department, district, and garrison in the provinces directly under the capital to recommend Xiaolian Fangzheng candidates, grant them sixth-rank ceremonial robes, and hold them in reserve for summons and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Integrity and Upright Conduct examination began in the sixty-first year of the Kangxi reign. When the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne, he ordered every prefecture, department, district, and garrison in the metropolitan provinces to recommend candidates, confer sixth-rank ceremonial insignia upon them, and hold them ready for imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，詔曰：「國家敦勵風俗，首重賢良。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, an edict stated: "The state, in earnestly encouraging custom, places prime importance on the worthy and good.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign, an edict declared: "In earnestly promoting public morals, the state above all values the worthy and upright.

sentences.zh: 前詔舉孝廉方正，距今數月，未有疏聞。

translations.literal: The previous edict calling for Xiaolian Fangzheng recommendations was issued several months ago, yet no memorial has been received.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier edict calling for Filial Integrity and Upright Conduct recommendations was issued several months ago, yet no memorial has yet been received.

sentences.zh: 恐有司怠於採訪，雖有端方之品，無由上達。

translations.literal: I fear that local officials have been lax in seeking them out, so that even upright and proper men cannot have their merits reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that local officials have been negligent in searching them out, so that even men of upright character cannot have their merits reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 各督、撫速遵前詔，確訪舉奏。」

translations.literal: Each governor-general and governor should promptly obey the previous edict, thoroughly investigate, and memorialize with recommendations."
translations.idiomatic: Each governor-general and governor should promptly carry out the previous edict, conduct thorough investigations, and submit recommendations by memorial."

sentences.zh: 尋浙江、直隸、福建、廣西各薦舉二員，用知縣；

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, Zhejiang, Zhili, Fujian, and Guangxi each recommended two candidates, who were appointed county magistrates;
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, Zhejiang, Zhili, Fujian, and Guangxi each recommended two men, who were appointed county magistrates;

sentences.zh: 年五十五以上者，用知州。

translations.literal: Those fifty-five years of age or older were appointed prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Those fifty-five years of age or older were appointed as prefects.

sentences.zh: 其後歷朝御極，皆恩詔薦舉以為常。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever a new emperor ascended the throne in successive reigns, grace edicts calling for recommendations became standard practice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever a new emperor ascended the throne, grace edicts calling for such recommendations became routine.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，刑部侍郎勵宗萬言：「孝廉方正之舉，稍有冒濫，即有屈抑。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, Li Zongwan, vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, stated: "In the Xiaolian Fangzheng recommendations, where there is the slightest abuse and flooding of candidates, worthy men are inevitably suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, Li Zongwan, vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, said: "In the Filial Integrity and Upright Conduct selections, even a little favoritism and abuse means worthy men are passed over.

sentences.zh: 從前選舉各官，鮮克公當。

translations.literal: Among the officials selected in the past, few could be fair and proper.
translations.idiomatic: Of the officials chosen in the past, few were selected fairly or appropriately.

sentences.zh: 非鄉井有力之富豪，即宮牆有名之學霸。

translations.literal: They were either powerful local wealthy men, or famous academic bullies within the school walls.
translations.idiomatic: They were either powerful local magnates or celebrated bullies of the examination halls.

sentences.zh: 迨服官後，庸者或以劣黜，黠者或以贓敗。

translations.literal: Once they took office, the mediocre were dismissed for incompetence, and the cunning were ruined by corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, the mediocre were dismissed for incompetence, and the shrewd were disgraced by corruption.

sentences.zh: 請慎選舉，以重名器。」

translations.literal: I request that selections be made carefully, to honor the prestige of office."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that selections be made with greater care, so as to preserve the dignity of public office."

sentences.zh: 吏部議准府、州、縣、衛保舉孝廉方正，應由地方紳士里黨合辭公舉，州、縣官採訪公評，詳稽事實。

translations.literal: The Board of Civil Appointments deliberated and approved: for recommendations of Xiaolian Fangzheng by prefectures, departments, districts, and garrisons, local gentry and community groups should jointly submit a public nomination; district and prefectural officials should investigate and assess public opinion, and thoroughly verify the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Civil Appointments approved the following: recommendations of Filial Integrity and Upright Conduct candidates from prefectures, departments, districts, and garrisons should come from joint public nomination by local gentry and neighbors; district and prefectural officials should investigate public reputation and verify the facts in detail.

sentences.zh: 所舉或系生員，會學官考覈，申送大吏，覈實具題，給六品章服榮身。

translations.literal: If the recommended person was a licentiate, the educational officials would join in examination and verification; the case would be forwarded to higher officials, verified and reported in a memorial, and sixth-rank ceremonial robes would be granted as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: If the nominee was a licentiate, the educational officials would examine him jointly; the case would then be forwarded to higher authorities, verified and reported in a memorial, and sixth-rank ceremonial insignia would be granted as a personal honor.

sentences.zh: 果有德行才識兼優者，督、撫逾格保薦赴部，九卿、翰、詹、科、道公同驗看，候旨擢用。

translations.literal: If there were truly those combining virtue, conduct, talent, and insight, governors-general and governors could exceptionally recommend them to the ministry; the Nine Ministers, Hanlin and Grand Secretariat officials, censors, and surveillance commissioners would jointly inspect them, awaiting imperial instruction for promotion and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: If a candidate truly combined virtue, conduct, talent, and judgment, the governor-general or governor might exceptionally recommend him to the ministry; the Nine Ministers, Hanlin and Grand Secretariat officials, censors, and surveillance commissioners would jointly inspect him and await imperial orders for promotion.

sentences.zh: 濫舉者罪之。

translations.literal: Those who recommended unqualified persons would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who made improper recommendations would be punished.

sentences.zh: 五年，定考試例。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, examination regulations were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign, examination regulations were established.

sentences.zh: 除樸實拘謹、無他技能、不能應試者，例予頂戴，不送部外，其膺薦赴部者，驗看後，試以時務策、箋、奏各一於太和殿門內。

translations.literal: Except for those who were plain, cautious, and without other skills and could not take the examination—who were routinely granted official insignia without being sent to the ministry—those recommended and sent to the ministry, after inspection, were tested with one policy essay on current affairs, one formal memorial of felicitation, and one memorial submission each, inside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Except for plain, cautious men without other skills who could not sit for the examination and were routinely granted official insignia without being sent to the ministry, those recommended to the capital were inspected and then tested inside the Gate of Supreme Harmony with one policy essay on current affairs, one formal felicitation, and one memorial each.

sentences.zh: 道光間，改於保和殿，如考試御史例。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang reign, the venue was changed to the Hall of Preserving Harmony, following the precedent for censor examinations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign, the examination was moved to the Hall of Preserving Harmony, following the precedent used for censor examinations.

sentences.zh: 同治初元，明詔選舉，又以知縣黎庶昌條陳，諭令在京四品以上，在外督、撫、學政，各舉所知，不限紳士、布衣，以躬行實踐為先，毋得專取文詞藻麗者，濫膺盛典。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, with a clear edict on selection, and further prompted by a memorial from the county magistrate Li Shuchang, officials of fourth rank and above in the capital and governors-general, governors, and education commissioners in the provinces were ordered each to recommend those they knew, without limitation to gentry or commoners; personal conduct and practical achievement should come first, and one must not select solely for ornate literary style, lest one unworthily receive this grand honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, after a clear edict on selection and a memorial from the county magistrate Li Shuchang, officials of fourth rank and above in the capital and governors-general, governors, and education commissioners in the provinces were ordered each to recommend men they knew, whether gentry or commoners; personal conduct and practical achievement were to come first, and candidates were not to be chosen merely for ornate prose, lest they unworthily receive so great an honor.

sentences.zh: 其有年登耄耋，或誠樸無華，足為里閭矜式，不原來京者，州縣官歲時存問，賜以酒米。

translations.literal: For those who had reached extreme old age, or were sincere and plain without ornament, sufficient to serve as models for their neighborhoods, and who did not wish to come to the capital, district and prefectural officials would visit them at the seasonal festivals and grant them wine and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had reached great old age, or who were sincere and unadorned and worthy to serve as models for their communities yet did not wish to come to the capital, were to be visited by district and prefectural officials at the seasonal festivals and granted wine and grain.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，定自恩詔日起，予限八年，人文到部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, it was fixed that from the date of the grace edict, an eight-year limit was granted for recommended candidates to reach the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Guangxu reign, it was fixed that from the date of the grace edict, candidates would be allowed eight years to reach the ministry.

sentences.zh: 每年二月、八月，各會驗奏考一次，逾限者止許章服榮身，不得與考。

translations.literal: Each February and August, they would assemble for inspection, reporting, and examination once; those who exceeded the time limit were permitted only ceremonial robes as an honor and could not participate in the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Each February and August they would assemble for inspection, reporting, and examination; those who exceeded the time limit were allowed ceremonial insignia as a personal honor only and could not sit for the examination.

sentences.zh: 初制授官用知州、知縣，厥後薦舉人眾，乃推廣用途，分別以知縣、直隸州州同、州判、佐雜等官及教職用。

translations.literal: Under the original system, appointments were as prefects and county magistrates; thereafter, as recommendations grew numerous, uses were broadened, and appointments were respectively made as county magistrates, sub-prefects of directly administered departments, vice-prefects, various assistant and miscellaneous officials, and educational posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original system, appointees were made prefects or county magistrates; later, as recommendations multiplied, appointments were broadened to include county magistrates, sub-prefects of directly administered departments, vice-prefects, various assistant and miscellaneous posts, and educational offices.

sentences.zh: 知縣得缺視拔貢，教職視大挑二等舉人，餘均分省試用序補。

translations.literal: Vacancies for county magistrate were treated like those for specially promoted tribute students; educational posts like second-tier juren from the Grand Selection; the rest were assigned for trial service by province in order of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies for county magistrate were filled on the same terms as specially promoted tribute students; educational posts on the same terms as second-tier juren from the Grand Selection; all others were assigned for provincial trial service in order.

sentences.zh: 歷朝以來，有司奉行，第應故事。

translations.literal: Throughout successive reigns, local officials carried this out merely as a matter of routine precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout successive reigns, local officials carried it out merely as a matter of routine.

sentences.zh: 徇情冒濫之弊，台諫屢以上聞。

translations.literal: The abuse of favoritism and false recommendations was repeatedly reported to the throne by censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: The evils of favoritism and abuse were repeatedly reported to the throne by censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 惟嘉慶朝湖南嚴如煜以對策第一，召見授知縣。

translations.literal: Only in the Jiaqing reign did Yan Ruyu of Hunan, ranking first in the policy examination, receive an audience and appointment as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Jiaqing reign did Yan Ruyu of Hunan, who ranked first in the policy examination, receive an audience and appointment as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐朝湖南羅澤南以書生率湘勇越境剿賊，皆以勛績見稱於時。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng reign, Luo Zenan of Hunan, a scholar leading Hunan braves across borders to suppress bandits—both were renowned at the time for their meritorious achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng reign, Luo Zenan of Hunan, a scholar who led Hunan militia across provincial borders to suppress bandits—both men were renowned at the time for their achievements.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，各省所舉多至百數十人，少亦數十人，詔飭嚴行甄覈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign, recommendations from the provinces often reached over a hundred, or at least several dozen; an edict ordered strict screening and verification.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign, provincial recommendations often ran to well over a hundred men, or at least several dozen; an edict ordered strict screening and verification.

sentences.zh: 選舉之風，於斯濫矣。

translations.literal: The practice of recommendation had by then become thoroughly corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: By then the practice of recommendation had become thoroughly corrupt.

sentences.zh: 清代科目取士外，或徵之遺佚，或擢之廉能，或舉之文學，或拔之戎行，或辟之幕職，薦擢一途，得人稱盛，有足述焉。

translations.literal: Beyond the civil service examination system of the Qing, there were also summons of those overlooked, promotion of the incorruptible and capable, recommendation for literary talent, selection from military service, and recruitment to secretarial posts—the path of recommendation and promotion produced many outstanding men, and is worth relating.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the regular examination system, the Qing also summoned overlooked talent, promoted the incorruptible and capable, recommended men of letters, selected officers from the ranks, and recruited secretarial staff; this path of recommendation and promotion produced many outstanding men and is well worth recounting.

sentences.zh: 太祖肇興東土，選拔英豪以輔大業，委輅杖策之士咸與擢用，或招直文館，或留預帷幄。

translations.literal: When the Taizu founder rose in the eastern lands, he selected heroes to assist the great enterprise; scholars who laid aside their carriages and canes were all promoted and employed, some recruited to the Literary Hall, others retained to participate in strategic counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu founder rose in the eastern lands, he selected heroes to assist the great enterprise; scholars who had laid aside carriage and cane were all promoted and employed, some recruited to the Literary Hall and others retained for counsel in the command tent.

sentences.zh: 乙卯十一月，諭群臣曰：「國務殷繁，必得賢才眾多，量能授職。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the yimao year, he instructed the ministers: "State affairs are numerous and pressing; many talented men must be obtained, and posts assigned according to capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the yimao year, he told his ministers: "State affairs are pressing; many talented men must be found, and posts assigned according to their capacity.

sentences.zh: 勇能攻戰者，宜治軍；

translations.literal: Those brave and able in attack and battle should command armies;
translations.idiomatic: Those brave and skilled in battle should command armies;

sentences.zh: 才優經濟者，宜理國；

translations.literal: Those outstanding in statecraft should govern the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Those outstanding in statecraft should govern the realm;

sentences.zh: 博通典故者，宜諮得失；

translations.literal: Those broadly versed in historical precedents should be consulted on gains and losses;
translations.idiomatic: Those broadly versed in historical precedent should be consulted on policy;

sentences.zh: 嫺習儀文者，宜襄典禮。

translations.literal: Those skilled in ritual and ceremonial texts should assist in rites.
translations.idiomatic: Those skilled in ritual and ceremonial forms should assist in state ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 當隨地旁求，俾列庶位。」

translations.literal: One should seek widely in every place, so that they may fill the various posts."
translations.idiomatic: Talent should be sought everywhere, so that men may fill every post."

sentences.zh: 時削平諸國，設八旗制，需才亟。

translations.literal: At that time, as the various states were being subdued and the Eight Banners system established, talent was urgently needed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the dynasty was subduing rival states and establishing the Eight Banners system, and talent was urgently needed.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，首任儒臣范文程領樞密重事。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he first entrusted the Confucian minister Fan Wencheng with weighty affairs of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Taiji took the throne, he first entrusted the Confucian minister Fan Wencheng with the weightiest affairs of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，甲喇章京硃繼文子延慶上書，言：「我朝攻城破敵、斬將搴旗者不乏人，守境治民、安內攘外者未多見。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong, the jalan ejen Zhu Jiwen's son Yanqing submitted a memorial stating: "In our dynasty there is no lack of men who storm cities, defeat enemies, behead generals, and capture banners; but men who guard the borders, govern the people, and pacify within while repelling without are not often seen."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiancong, Yanqing, son of the jalan ejen Zhu Jiwen, submitted a memorial stating: "In our dynasty there is no lack of men who storm cities, defeat enemies, behead generals, and capture banners, but men who guard the borders, govern the people, and pacify within while repelling threats from without are rarely seen."

sentences.zh: 因疏舉漢人陳極新、刑部啟心郎申朝紀，足備任使。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended in a memorial the Han Chinese Chen Jixin and the vice minister of punishments Shen Chaoji as fully fit for employment.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore recommended in a memorial the Han Chinese Chen Jixin and Shen Chaoji, vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, as fully fit for service.

sentences.zh: 帝召延慶等御前，溫諭褒獎。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yanqing and the others before the throne and warmly praised and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yanqing and the others before the throne and warmly praised and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 命延慶、極新，文館錄用；

translations.literal: He ordered Yanqing and Jixin enrolled in the Literary Hall;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yanqing and Jixin enrolled in the Literary Hall;

sentences.zh: 朝紀仍任部事。

translations.literal: Chaoji continued to serve in his ministry post.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoji continued in his ministry post.

sentences.zh: 九年，諭滿、漢、蒙古各官，薦舉人才，不限已仕、未仕，牒送吏、禮二部，具名以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict instructed Manchu, Han, and Mongol officials to recommend talent without limiting those already in office or not yet in office; memorials were to be sent to the Boards of Civil Appointments and Rites with names listed for report.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, an edict instructed Manchu, Han, and Mongol officials to recommend talent whether already in office or not; their names were to be sent in memorials to the Boards of Civil Appointments and Rites.

sentences.zh: 直文館寧完我言：「古者薦舉之條，功罪連坐，所以杜弊端、防冒濫。

translations.literal: Ning Wanwo of the Literary Hall stated: "In antiquity the rules for recommendation imposed joint responsibility for merit and guilt, thereby blocking abuses and preventing false recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Wanwo of the Literary Hall said: "In antiquity the rules for recommendation imposed joint responsibility for merit and guilt, thereby blocking abuses and preventing false nominations.

sentences.zh: 請自後所舉之人，或功或罪，舉者同之。

translations.literal: I request that hereafter, for those recommended, whether they achieve merit or commit offense, the recommender share the same fate.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter, for anyone recommended, whether he achieves merit or commits offense, the recommender share the same fate.

sentences.zh: 若其人砥行於厥初，改節於末路，許舉者隨時檢舉，免連坐。」

translations.literal: If the person was upright at first but changed his conduct at the end, the recommender may report this at any time and be exempt from joint responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: If a man was upright at first but changed his conduct later, the recommender may report this at any time and be exempt from joint punishment."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎中原，順治初元，遣官徵訪遺賢，車軺絡繹。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor established the capital in the Central Plains, in the first year of Shunzhi, officials were dispatched to seek out overlooked worthies, and mission carts came and went in continuous succession.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shunzhi Emperor established the dynasty in the Central Plains, in the first year of his reign officials were dispatched to seek out overlooked worthies, and mission carts came and went without pause.

sentences.zh: 吏部詳察履歷，確覈才品，促令來京。

translations.literal: The Board of Civil Appointments examined biographies in detail, verified talent and character, and urged them to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Civil Appointments examined their records in detail, verified their talent and character, and urged them to come to the capital.

sentences.zh: 並行撫、按，境內隱逸、賢良，逐一啟薦，以憑徵擢。

translations.literal: At the same time governors and surveillance commissioners were ordered that recluses and worthy men within their jurisdictions should each be reported and recommended for summons and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time governors and surveillance commissioners were ordered to recommend recluses and worthy men within their jurisdictions one by one for summons and promotion.

sentences.zh: 順天巡撫宋權陳治平三策，首廣羅賢才以佐上理，並薦故明薊遼總督王永吉等。

translations.literal: The Shuntian surveillance commissioner Song Quan presented three policies for good governance, the first calling for broadly gathering worthy talent to assist the ruler in governing, and also recommended the former Ming Jiliao governor-general Wang Yongji and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuntian surveillance commissioner Song Quan presented three policies for good governance, the first calling for broadly gathering worthy talent to assist the throne, and also recommended the former Ming Jiliao governor-general Wang Yongji and others.

sentences.zh: 詔廷臣各舉所知。

translations.literal: An edict ordered court officials each to recommend those they knew.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered court officials each to recommend men they knew.

sentences.zh: 一時明季故臣如謝升、馮銓、黨崇雅等，紛紛擢用。

translations.literal: For a time former Ming officials such as Xie Sheng, Feng Quan, and Dang Chongya were promoted and employed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: For a time former Ming officials such as Xie Sheng, Feng Quan, and Dang Chongya were promoted and employed in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 中外臣工啟薦除授得官者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Among officials at court and in the provinces who memorialized recommendations and received appointment, the number was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The number of officials at court and in the provinces who were recommended by memorial and appointed to office was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 嗣以廷臣所舉，類多明季舊吏廢員，未有肥遯隱逸逃名之士。

translations.literal: Subsequently, those recommended by court officials were mostly dismissed Ming-era old officials; there were no reclusive hermits who had withdrawn and shunned fame.
translations.idiomatic: Later it became clear that those recommended by court officials were mostly dismissed Ming-era old officials, and that there were no truly reclusive men who had withdrawn and shunned public life.

sentences.zh: 詔自今嚴責舉主，得人者優加進賢之賞，舛謬者嚴行連坐之罰。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on recommenders would be strictly held accountable: those who found good men would receive exceptional rewards for advancing the worthy, and those who erred would be strictly punished by joint responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that from then on recommenders would be strictly held accountable: those who found good men would receive exceptional rewards, and those who erred would be strictly punished by joint responsibility.

sentences.zh: 薦章止以履歷上聞，才品所宜，聽朝廷裁奪。

translations.literal: Recommendation memorials were to report only biographies upward; what talent and character were suitable would be left to the court's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendation memorials were to report only the candidate's record; whether his talent and character were suitable would be left to the court's judgment.

sentences.zh: 儻以貲郎雜流及黜革青衿、投閒武弁，妄充隱逸，咎有所歸。

translations.literal: If purchased-office holders and miscellaneous ranks, dismissed licentiates, or idle military officers were falsely passed off as recluses, blame would fall on the recommender.
translations.idiomatic: If purchased-office holders, dismissed licentiates, or idle military officers were falsely passed off as recluses, blame would fall on the recommender.

sentences.zh: 若畏避連坐，緘默不舉，治以蔽賢罪。

translations.literal: If out of fear of joint responsibility one kept silent and did not recommend, one would be punished for concealing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: If out of fear of joint punishment one kept silent and did not recommend anyone, one would be punished for concealing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 二年，陝西、江南平，詔徵山林隱逸，並故明文、武進士、舉人。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Shaanxi and Jiangnan were pacified, an edict summoned recluses in mountains and forests, as well as former Ming civil and military jinshi and juren.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after Shaanxi and Jiangnan were pacified, an edict summoned recluses in mountains and forests, as well as former Ming civil and military jinshi and juren.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫李之奇以保薦濫及貲郎，詔旨切責。

translations.literal: The Shandong governor Li Zhiqi was sharply rebuked by imperial edict for recommending purchased-office holders among the selections.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong governor Li Zhiqi was sharply rebuked by imperial edict for recommending purchased-office holders among his nominees.

sentences.zh: 十三年，江南巡撫張中元薦故明進士陸貽吉、於沚，帝親試之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Jiangnan governor Zhang Zhongyuan recommended the former Ming jinshi Lu Yiji and Yu Zhi; the emperor personally examined them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, the Jiangnan governor Zhang Zhongyuan recommended the former Ming jinshi Lu Yiji and Yu Zhi, and the emperor personally examined them.

sentences.zh: 是年復詔各省舉奏地方人才，給事中梁鋐言：「皇上寤寐求才，詔舉山林隱逸，應聘之士，自不乏人。

translations.literal: That year an edict again ordered the provinces to recommend local talent by memorial. The supervising secretary Liang Hong stated: "Your Majesty seeks talent day and night; the edict summoning recluses in mountains and forests has surely drawn many respondents.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict again ordered the provinces to recommend local talent by memorial. The supervising secretary Liang Hong said: "Your Majesty seeks talent day and night; the edict summoning recluses in mountains and forests has surely drawn many respondents.

sentences.zh: 然採訪未確，有負盛舉。

translations.literal: Yet the investigations have not been thorough, failing this grand undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the investigations have not been thorough, and the grand undertaking has fallen short.

sentences.zh: 如江南舉呂陽，授監司，未幾以贓敗；

translations.literal: For example, Jiangnan recommended Lü Yang, who was appointed a surveillance commissioner; before long he was ruined by corruption;
translations.idiomatic: For example, Jiangnan recommended Lü Yang, who was appointed a surveillance commissioner; before long he was ruined by corruption;

sentences.zh: 山東舉王運熙，授科員，未有建明，以計典去。

translations.literal: Shandong recommended Wang Yunxi, who was appointed a censor; he made no notable contribution and was removed in the regular evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong recommended Wang Yunxi, who was appointed a censor; he made no notable contribution and was removed in the regular evaluation.

sentences.zh: 呂陽等豈真抱匡濟之才，不過為梯榮之藉耳。

translations.literal: Were men like Lü Yang truly possessed of talent to save the realm? They were merely using the opportunity as a ladder to glory.
translations.idiomatic: Were men like Lü Yang truly possessed of talent to save the realm? They were merely using the opportunity as a ladder to advancement.

sentences.zh: 山林者何？

translations.literal: What are "mountains and forests"?
translations.idiomatic: What are "mountains and forests"?

sentences.zh: 謂遠於朝市也。

translations.literal: They mean being far from court and market.
translations.idiomatic: They mean being far from court and the bustle of public life.

sentences.zh: 隱逸者何？

translations.literal: What is "reclusion"?
translations.idiomatic: What is "reclusion"?

sentences.zh: 謂異於趨競也。

translations.literal: It means being unlike those who scramble for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: It means being unlike those who scramble for advancement.

sentences.zh: 必得其人，乃當其位。

translations.literal: Only when the right person is found should the post be filled.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the right person is found should the post be filled.

sentences.zh: 請飭詳加採訪。」

translations.literal: I request that thorough investigation be ordered."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a thorough investigation be ordered."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 順、康間，海內大師宿儒，以名節相高。

translations.literal: Between the Shunzhi and Kangxi reigns, the great masters and senior Confucians throughout the realm held one another in esteem for integrity and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Shunzhi and Kangxi reigns, the great masters and senior Confucians throughout the realm held one another in esteem for integrity and principle.

sentences.zh: 或廷臣交章論薦，疆吏備禮敦促，堅臥不起。

translations.literal: Some, though court officials submitted memorial after memorial recommending them and frontier officials came with full ceremony to urge them, steadfastly remained in bed and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Some, though court officials submitted memorial after memorial recommending them and provincial officials came with full ceremony to urge them, steadfastly refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 如孫奇逢、李顒、黃宗羲輩，天子知不可致，為嘆息不置，僅命督、撫抄錄著書送京師。

translations.literal: Men such as Sun Qifeng, Li Yong, and Huang Zongxi—the Son of Heaven knew they could not be summoned, sighed repeatedly without cease, and merely ordered governors-general and governors to copy their writings and send them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Sun Qifeng, Li Yong, and Huang Zongxi could not be summoned; the emperor sighed repeatedly in regret and merely ordered governors-general and governors to copy their writings and send them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，孝康皇后升祔禮成，頒詔天下，命有司舉才品優長、山林隱逸之士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, when the rites for enshrining Empress Xiaokang were completed, an edict was promulgated throughout the realm ordering officials to recommend men of outstanding talent and character among recluses in mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Kangxi reign, when the rites for enshrining Empress Xiaokang were completed, an edict was promulgated throughout the realm ordering officials to recommend men of outstanding talent and character among recluses in mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 自後歷朝推恩之典，雖如例行，實應者寡。

translations.literal: Thereafter, grace edicts of successive reigns, though observed as routine, drew few actual respondents.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, grace edicts of successive reigns, though observed as routine, drew few actual respondents.

sentences.zh: 初制，督、撫升遷離任時，薦舉人才一次。

translations.literal: Under the original system, when governors-general and governors were promoted or left office, they recommended talent once.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original system, when a governor-general or governor was promoted or left office, he recommended talent once.

sentences.zh: 嗣令歲一薦舉，部議大省限十人，小省限三四人，後復改二年薦舉一次。

translations.literal: Subsequently it was ordered that recommendations be made once a year; the ministry deliberated that large provinces were limited to ten persons and small provinces to three or four; later this was changed again to one recommendation every two years.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was ordered that recommendations be made once a year; the ministry set a limit of ten men for large provinces and three or four for small ones; still later this was changed to one recommendation every two years.

sentences.zh: 自順治十八年停差巡按，乃定各省巡撫應舉方面有司、佐貳、教官員額，總漕、總河應薦方面有司、佐貳額，亦著為例。

translations.literal: From the eighteenth year of Shunzhi, when the dispatch of surveillance commissioners was suspended, quotas were fixed for provincial governors to recommend provincial officials, deputies, and educational officers, and for the grain transport and river conservancy commissioners to recommend provincial officials and deputies; these too were established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From the eighteenth year of the Shunzhi reign, when the dispatch of surveillance commissioners was suspended, quotas were fixed for provincial governors to recommend provincial officials, deputies, and educational officers, and for the grain transport and river conservancy commissioners to recommend provincial officials and deputies; these too were established as precedent.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，御史張吉午奏：「三年考滿之法，一、二等稱職者，即系薦舉，請罷督、撫二年薦舉例。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, the censor Zhang Jiwu memorialized: "Under the three-year evaluation system, those rated first or second rank as competent are already recommendations; I request that the governors' biennial recommendation precedent be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Kangxi reign, the censor Zhang Jiwu memorialized: "Under the three-year evaluation system, officials rated first or second rank as competent are already being recommended; I ask that the governors' biennial recommendation precedent be abolished."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 六年，停考滿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the evaluation system was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the evaluation system was suspended.

sentences.zh: 用給事中李宗孔言復薦舉，與卓異並行。

translations.literal: Following the supervising secretary Li Zongkong's proposal, recommendations were restored and carried out in parallel with outstanding-performance designations.
translations.idiomatic: Following the supervising secretary Li Zongkong's proposal, recommendations were restored and carried out alongside outstanding-performance designations.

sentences.zh: 先是漕、河薦舉例停。

translations.literal: Previously the recommendation precedent for grain transport and river conservancy had been suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the recommendation precedent for grain transport and river conservancy had been suspended.

sentences.zh: 十二年，漕督帥顏保請復舊例，每年得舉劾屬吏示勸懲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the grain transport commissioner Shuai Yanbao requested restoration of the old precedent, whereby each year he could recommend and impeach subordinate officials to encourage the good and punish the bad.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the grain transport commissioner Shuai Yanbao requested restoration of the old precedent, whereby each year he could recommend and impeach subordinate officials as reward and warning.

sentences.zh: 部議行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry deliberated and approved.

sentences.zh: 因疏薦糧道範周、遲日巽、知縣吳興祚。

translations.literal: Through a memorial he recommended the grain-route intendant Fan Zhou, Chi Rixun, and the county magistrate Wu Xingzuo.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he recommended the grain-route intendant Fan Zhou, Chi Rixun, and the county magistrate Wu Xingzuo.

sentences.zh: 詔擢興祚福建按察使。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Xingzuo to Fujian surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Wu Xingzuo to Fujian surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，銳意整飭吏治，屢詔群臣薦舉天下廉能官。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor personally took power, he was keen to rectify official governance and repeatedly issued edicts ordering the ministers to recommend incorruptible and capable officials throughout the realm.
