translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor personally took power, he was keen to rectify official governance and repeatedly issued edicts ordering his ministers to recommend incorruptible and capable officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十八年，左都御史魏象樞疏薦清廉，原任侍郎高珩、達哈塔、雷虎、班迪，大理卿瑚密色，侍讀蕭維豫，郎中宋文運，布政使畢振姬，知縣張沐、陸隴其等十人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the left censor-in-chief Wei Xiangshu memorialized recommending ten men for incorruptibility: the former vice ministers Gao Heng, Dahata, Lei Hu, and Bandi; the chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review Humise; the Hanlin reader Xiao Weiyu; the bureau director Song Wenyun; the provincial treasurer Bi Zhenji; and the county magistrates Zhang Mu and Lu Longqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, the left censor-in-chief Wei Xiangshu memorialized recommending ten men for incorruptibility: the former vice ministers Gao Heng, Dahata, Lei Hu, and Bandi; the chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review Humise; the Hanlin reader Xiao Weiyu; the bureau director Song Wenyun; the provincial treasurer Bi Zhenji; and the county magistrates Zhang Mu and Lu Longqi.

sentences.zh: 得旨分別錄用。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript ordered them appointed according to their respective merits.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript ordered them appointed according to their respective merits.

sentences.zh: 並諭陸隴其廉能之員，宜任繁劇，如直隸清苑、江蘇無錫等縣，庶可表見其才。

translations.literal: Also ordered that officials of Lu Longqi's integrity and ability should be assigned demanding duties, such as Qingyuan County in Zhili and Wuxi County in Jiangsu, so that their talents might be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also directed that officials noted for integrity and ability like Lu Longqi should be placed in demanding posts—counties such as Qingyuan in Zhili and Wuxi in Jiangsu—where their talents could be fully displayed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，福建巡撫吳興祚薦按察使于成龍天下廉能第一，遷布政使，尋擢直隸巡撫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Fujian governor Wu Xingzuo recommended surveillance commissioner Yu Chenglong as first in the empire in integrity and ability; he was transferred to provincial treasurer, and soon promoted to governor of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, the governor of Fujian, Wu Xingzuo, recommended the surveillance commissioner Yu Chenglong as the most incorruptible and capable official in the empire; Yu was transferred to provincial treasurer and soon promoted to governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十年入覲，帝溫諭褒美。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he entered court for audience; the emperor warmly addressed him with praise.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court for audience in the twentieth year, the emperor received him warmly and spoke words of praise.

sentences.zh: 問屬吏中亦有清廉者否？

translations.literal: He asked whether among his subordinate officials there were also incorruptible ones.
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether any of his subordinate officials were also known for incorruptibility.

sentences.zh: 成龍以知縣謝錫袞、同知何如玉、羅京對。

translations.literal: Chenglong answered with the county magistrate Xie Xigun and the sub-prefects He Ruyu and Luo Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong named the county magistrate Xie Xigun and the sub-prefects He Ruyu and Luo Jing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，調成龍兩江總督。

translations.literal: Before long, Chenglong was transferred to governor-general of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Chenglong was transferred to governor-general of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，疏薦直隸守道董秉忠、通州知州于成龍、南路通判陳大棟、柏鄉知縣邵嗣堯、阜城知縣王燮、高陽知縣孫宏業、霸州州判衛濟賢，並堪大用。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, he memorialized recommending Zhili circuit intendant Dong Bingzhong, Tongzhou prefect Yu Chenglong, southern route sub-prefect Chen Dadong, Baixiang county magistrate Shao Siyao, Fucheng county magistrate Wang Xie, Gaoyang county magistrate Sun Hongye, and Bazhou assistant prefect Wei Jixian, all fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure, he memorialized recommending the Zhili circuit intendant Dong Bingzhong, the Tongzhou prefect Yu Chenglong, the southern route sub-prefect Chen Dadong, and the county magistrates Shao Siyao of Baixiang, Wang Xie of Fucheng, and Sun Hongye of Gaoyang, together with the Bazhou assistant prefect Wei Jixian—all of whom he deemed fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 會江寧知府缺，詔即以通州知州于成龍擢補。

translations.literal: When a vacancy arose for prefect of Jiangning, an edict immediately promoted and appointed the Tongzhou prefect Yu Chenglong to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Jiangning prefect fell vacant, an edict immediately promoted the Tongzhou prefect Yu Chenglong to fill it.

sentences.zh: 不數年，擢直隸巡撫。

translations.literal: Within a few years he was promoted to governor of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he was promoted to governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 同時兩于成龍，先後汲引，並以清操特邀帝眷，時論稱之。

translations.literal: At the same time there were two Yu Chenglongs; each in turn drew the other up, and both, by their incorruptible conduct, specially won the emperor's favor; contemporary opinion praised them.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there were two officials named Yu Chenglong; each in turn drew the other upward, and both won the emperor's special favor through their incorruptible conduct—contemporary opinion praised them warmly.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，諭部臣保舉應補關差，僉以「有才及謹慎者不乏人，而操守實難知」對。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the emperor instructed ministry officials to recommend candidates for vacant capital posts; all replied, "There is no lack of men of talent and prudence, but integrity is truly hard to know."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the emperor instructed ministry officials to recommend candidates for vacant capital posts; they all replied that there was no lack of talented and prudent men, but that integrity was truly hard to assess.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「清操如何可廢？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How can incorruptible conduct be set aside?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How can incorruptible conduct be set aside?

sentences.zh: 如郝浴居官甚好，猶侵蝕錢糧，魏象樞曾薦郝浴，此事安能豫知！

translations.literal: Take Hao Yu: he served very well in office, yet still embezzled tax grain; Wei Xiangshu once recommended Hao Yu—how could this have been foreknown!
translations.idiomatic: Take Hao Yu: he served very well in office, yet still embezzled tax grain; Wei Xiangshu once recommended him—how could anyone have foreseen that!

sentences.zh: 朕信部院堂官清操而委任之，堂官亦信司官而委任之。

translations.literal: I trust the integrity of ministry and yamen chief officials and entrust them with office; the chief officials likewise trust their bureau officials and entrust them with office.
translations.idiomatic: I trust the integrity of the chief officials of the ministries and yamens and entrust them with office; those chief officials likewise trust their subordinate bureau officials and entrust them in turn.

sentences.zh: 但將有守之人舉出，被舉者自能效力。」

translations.literal: Simply recommend men of integrity; those recommended will naturally exert themselves in service."
translations.idiomatic: Simply recommend men of proven integrity; those recommended will naturally serve effectively."

sentences.zh: 是年九卿、詹事、科、道遵旨疏舉清廉：直隸巡撫格爾古德，吏部郎中蘇赫、范承勛，江南學道趙侖，揚州知府崔華，兗州知府張鵬翮，靈壽知縣陸隴其等。

translations.literal: That year the nine ministers, grand tutors, censorate, and supervising secretaries, following the edict, memorialized recommending the incorruptible: Zhili governor Ge'ergude, Board of Civil Appointments bureau directors Suhe and Fan Chengxun, Jiangnan education intendant Zhao Lun, Yangzhou prefect Cui Hua, Yanzhou prefect Zhang Penghe, Lingshou county magistrate Lu Longqi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: That year the nine ministers, grand tutors, censorate, and supervising secretaries, following the edict, memorialized recommending incorruptible officials: the governor of Zhili Ge'ergude; the Board of Civil Appointments bureau directors Suhe and Fan Chengxun; the Jiangnan education intendant Zhao Lun; the Yangzhou prefect Cui Hua; the Yanzhou prefect Zhang Penghe; the Lingshou county magistrate Lu Longqi; and others.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，帝嘉直隸巡撫于成龍清廉，命九卿各舉廉吏如成龍者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the emperor praised the Zhili governor Yu Chenglong for incorruptibility and ordered the nine ministers each to recommend incorruptible officials like Chenglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, the emperor praised the governor of Zhili, Yu Chenglong, for his incorruptibility and ordered each of the nine ministers to recommend incorruptible officials like him.

sentences.zh: 大學士等薦雲貴總督范承勛、山西巡撫馬齊、四川巡撫姚締虞。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries and others recommended Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Fan Chengxun, Shanxi governor Ma Qi, and Sichuan governor Yao Diyu.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries and others recommended the Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Fan Chengxun, the Shanxi governor Ma Qi, and the Sichuan governor Yao Diyu.

sentences.zh: 帝謂承勛等居官皆優，但尚有勉強之意。

translations.literal: The emperor said that Fan Chengxun and the others all served excellently in office, but still showed something of forced effort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said that Fan Chengxun and the others all served well in office, but still showed something of forced effort in their conduct.

sentences.zh: 成龍則出自誠心，毫無瞻顧。

translations.literal: Chenglong, by contrast, acted from sincere heart, with no looking back in hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong, by contrast, acted from sincere conviction, with no hesitation or second thoughts.

sentences.zh: 命加成龍太子少保銜，以勸廉能。

translations.literal: An order added to Chenglong the nominal rank of junior guardian of the heir apparent, to encourage integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong was granted the nominal rank of junior guardian of the heir apparent, to encourage integrity and ability among officials.

sentences.zh: 四十年，敕總督郭琇、張鵬翮、桑額、華顯，巡撫彭鵬、李光地、徐潮薦道、府以下，知縣以上，清廉愛民者，勿計罣誤降罰，勿拘本省鄰屬，具以名聞。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, an edict ordered governors-general Guo Xiu, Zhang Penghe, Sang'e, and Hua Xian, and governors Peng Peng, Li Guangdi, and Xu Chao to recommend circuit officials and below and county magistrates and above who were incorruptible and loved the people; do not count demerits, errors, or demotions and punishments; do not restrict to one's own province or neighboring jurisdictions; report all names fully.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year, an edict ordered the governors-general Guo Xiu, Zhang Penghe, Sang'e, and Hua Xian and the governors Peng Peng, Li Guangdi, and Xu Chao to recommend officials from the circuit level down to the county magistrate level who were incorruptible and cared for the people—without regard to demerits, errors, or past demotions and punishments, and without restricting nominations to their own province or neighboring jurisdictions—and to report all names in full.

sentences.zh: 時天子廣厲風節，群士慕效，吏治丕變。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven broadly encouraged moral integrity; the multitude of officials admired and emulated it, and official governance was greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor broadly encouraged moral integrity; officials throughout the empire admired and emulated it, and governance was greatly transformed.

sentences.zh: 循吏被薦膺顯擢者，先後踵相接。

translations.literal: Honest local officials who were recommended and received conspicuous promotion followed one after another in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Honest local officials who were recommended and received conspicuous promotion followed one after another in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 先是廷臣會推廣西按察使缺，吏部侍郎胡簡敬，淮安人，以推舉淮揚道高成美違例獲譴，至是申禁九卿毋得保舉同鄉及本省官，復限每人歲舉毋逾十人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when court officials jointly recommended for the Guangxi surveillance commissioner vacancy, Board of Civil Appointments vice minister Hu Jianjing, a native of Huai'an, was punished for recommending Huai-Yang circuit intendant Gao Chengmei in violation of regulations; at this point it was announced that the nine ministers must not recommend men from their native place or their own province, and again each person was limited to no more than ten recommendations per year.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when court officials jointly recommended candidates for the vacant post of Guangxi surveillance commissioner, the Board of Civil Appointments vice minister Hu Jianjing, a native of Huai'an, was punished for recommending the Huai-Yang circuit intendant Gao Chengmei in violation of regulations; at this point it was announced that the nine ministers must not recommend men from their native place or their own province, and that each person was again limited to no more than ten recommendations per year.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，尚書趙申喬舉潮州知府張應詔能耐清貧，可為兩淮運使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, Minister Zhao Shenqiao recommended Chaozhou prefect Zhang Yingshao as able to endure poverty while remaining incorrupt, fit to serve as Liang-Huai transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year, Minister Zhao Shenqiao recommended the Chaozhou prefect Zhang Yingshao as a man able to endure poverty while remaining incorrupt, fit to serve as commissioner of Liang-Huai transport.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「清官不系貧富，張伯行家道甚饒，任所日用皆取諸其家，以為不清可乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Incorruptible officials are not tied to wealth or poverty. Zhang Bojia's family estate is very ample; all daily expenses at his post are taken from his household—can he therefore be deemed not incorrupt?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Incorruptible officials are not defined by wealth or poverty. Zhang Bojia's family estate is very ample, and all his daily expenses in office are paid from his own household—can he therefore be deemed corrupt?

sentences.zh: 一心為國即好官，或操守雖清，不能辦事，亦何裨於國？」

translations.literal: One who single-mindedly serves the state is a good official; or if one's conduct is incorrupt yet one cannot handle affairs, what benefit is there to the state?"
translations.idiomatic: An official who single-mindedly serves the state is a good official; but if one's conduct is incorrupt yet one cannot handle affairs, what benefit is there to the state?"

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗嗣位。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, the Shizong emperor succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year, the Shizong emperor succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「知人則哲，自古為難。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "To know men is to be wise—this has been difficult since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "To know men is to be wise—this has been difficult since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 朕臨御之初，簡用人才，或品行端方，或操守清廉，或才具敏練，諸大臣密奏所知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of my assuming rule, in selecting and employing talent, whether of upright character, incorruptible conduct, or keen and practiced ability, all ministers shall memorialize in secret those they know.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of my reign, in selecting and employing talent—whether for upright character, incorruptible conduct, or keen and practiced ability—all ministers were to memorialize in secret those they knew.

sentences.zh: 勿避嫌徇私，沽名市恩，有負諮詢。」

translations.literal: Do not avoid suspicion yet practice favoritism, or seek reputation and trade in favor, failing this consultation."
translations.idiomatic: Do not avoid suspicion yet practice favoritism, or seek reputation and trade in favor, betraying this consultation."

sentences.zh: 又以道、府、州、縣，親民要職，敕總督舉三員，巡撫舉二員，布、按各舉一員，將軍、提督亦得舉一員，密封奏聞。

translations.literal: Further, because circuit, prefecture, department, and county posts are key offices close to the people, governors-general were ordered to recommend three men, governors two men, provincial treasurers and surveillance commissioners one man each, and generals and provincial military commanders also one man each, reporting by sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also directed that, because circuit, prefecture, department, and county posts were key offices close to the people, governors-general were to recommend three men, governors two, provincial treasurers and surveillance commissioners one each, and generals and provincial military commanders one each, reporting by sealed memorial.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，以各省所舉未能稱旨，詔切責之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, because the recommendations from the provinces failed to satisfy the imperial intent, an edict sharply rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, because the recommendations from the provinces failed to satisfy the emperor's intent, an edict sharply rebuked the officials involved.

sentences.zh: 令各明舉一人，不得雷同。

translations.literal: Each was ordered clearly to recommend one person, with no identical submissions allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Each official was ordered clearly to recommend one person, with no identical submissions allowed.

sentences.zh: 時薦賢詔屢下，帝綜覈名實，賞罰必行。

translations.literal: At that time edicts recommending the worthy were repeatedly issued; the emperor comprehensively verified name against reality, and rewards and punishments were always carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time edicts calling for the recommendation of worthy men were repeatedly issued; the emperor comprehensively verified reputation against reality, and rewards and punishments were always enforced.

sentences.zh: 七年，以督、撫、布、按，為全省表率。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because governors-general, governors, provincial treasurers, and surveillance commissioners were the models for an entire province,
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, because governors-general, governors, provincial treasurers, and surveillance commissioners were the models for an entire province,

sentences.zh: 命京官學士、侍郎以上，外官籓、臬以上，各密保一人，不拘滿、漢，不限資格，即府、縣中有信其可任封疆大僚，亦許列薦剡。

translations.literal: an order directed that capital officials of bachelor and vice minister rank and above, and provincial officials of provincial treasurer and surveillance commissioner rank and above, each secretly recommend one person, without restriction as to Manchu or Han, without limit on qualifications; even among prefecture and county officials, if one believed someone fit for a great frontier post, listing him in a recommendation memorial was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that capital officials of bachelor and vice minister rank and above and provincial officials of provincial treasurer and surveillance commissioner rank and above each secretly recommend one person, without restriction as to Manchu or Han and without limit on qualifications; even among prefecture and county officials, if one believed someone fit for a great frontier post, listing him in a recommendation memorial was also permitted.

sentences.zh: 高宗重視親民之官，乾隆二年，諭仿雍正時例，督、撫、布、按，各密舉一、二人。

translations.literal: The Gaozong emperor attached importance to officials close to the people; in the second year of Qianlong, an edict ordered following the Yongzheng precedent: governors-general, governors, provincial treasurers, and surveillance commissioners each secretly recommended one or two men.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong emperor attached great importance to officials close to the people; in the second year of Qianlong, an edict ordered that governors-general, governors, provincial treasurers, and surveillance commissioners each secretly recommend one or two men, following the Yongzheng precedent.

sentences.zh: 次年，覆命大學士、九卿舉堪任道、府人員，露章啟奏。

translations.literal: The following year, a renewed order directed grand secretaries and the nine ministers to recommend men fit for circuit and prefecture posts, presenting open memorials to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, a renewed order directed the grand secretaries and the nine ministers to recommend men fit for circuit and prefecture posts, presenting open memorials to the throne.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔大學士舉編、檢能任知府者。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered grand secretaries to recommend compilers and revisers capable of serving as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, an edict ordered the grand secretaries to recommend compilers and revisers capable of serving as prefects.

sentences.zh: 十四年，命侍郎以上舉能任三品京堂者，尚書以上舉能任侍郎者。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, vice ministers and above were ordered to recommend men fit for third-rank capital posts; ministers and above were ordered to recommend men fit for vice minister posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, vice ministers and above were ordered to recommend men fit for third-rank capital posts, while ministers and above were ordered to recommend men fit for vice minister posts.

sentences.zh: 其時明揚、密保，並行不廢。

translations.literal: At that time open recommendation and secret recommendation proceeded in parallel without being abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time open recommendation and secret recommendation proceeded in parallel, neither being abolished.

sentences.zh: 科、道行取，自康熙七年復舊制。

translations.literal: Selection of censorate and secretariat officials by imperial appointment resumed the old system from the seventh year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The selection of censorate and secretariat officials by imperial appointment resumed the old system from the seventh year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 詔督、撫舉親民之官，賢能夙著者，親加選用。

translations.literal: An edict ordered governors-general and governors to recommend officials close to the people whose virtue and ability had long been outstanding, to be personally selected and employed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered governors-general and governors to recommend officials close to the people whose virtue and ability had long been outstanding, for the emperor's personal selection and appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，詔九卿各舉所知。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, an edict ordered the nine ministers each to recommend those they knew.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, an edict ordered each of the nine ministers to recommend those they knew.

sentences.zh: 尚書王騭舉清苑知縣邵嗣堯，李天馥舉三河知縣彭鵬、靈壽知縣陸隴其，徐元文舉麻城知縣趙蒼璧。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Ji recommended Qingyuan county magistrate Shao Siyao; Li Tianfu recommended Sanhe county magistrate Peng Peng and Lingshou county magistrate Lu Longqi; Xu Yuanwen recommended Macheng county magistrate Zhao Cangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Ji recommended the Qingyuan county magistrate Shao Siyao; Li Tianfu recommended the Sanhe county magistrate Peng Peng and the Lingshou county magistrate Lu Longqi; and Xu Yuanwen recommended the Macheng county magistrate Zhao Cangbi.

sentences.zh: 及廷推時，帝復問左都御史陳廷敬，廉者為誰？

translations.literal: At the time of court joint recommendation, the emperor again asked the left censor-in-chief Chen Tingjing, "Who are the incorruptible ones?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time of court joint recommendation, the emperor again asked the left censor-in-chief Chen Tingjing who the incorruptible officials were.

sentences.zh: 廷敬亦以隴其、嗣堯天下清官為言。

translations.literal: Tingjing also spoke of Lu Longqi and Siyao as the empire's incorruptible officials.
translations.idiomatic: Tingjing also named Lu Longqi and Shao Siyao as the empire's foremost incorruptible officials.

sentences.zh: 時同舉十二人，俱用科、道。

translations.literal: At that time twelve men were jointly recommended, all appointed to censorate and secretariat posts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time twelve men were jointly recommended, all appointed to posts in the censorate and secretariat.

sentences.zh: 得人為最。

translations.literal: Finding the right men was paramount.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the right men was paramount.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，吏部奏請行取，高宗命尚書、都御史、侍郎於各部屬，州、縣內，秉公保舉，如康熙二十九年例。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong, the Board of Civil Appointments memorialized requesting imperial selection; the Gaozong emperor ordered ministers, censor-in-chiefs, and vice ministers fairly to recommend from among their department subordinates and from within prefectures and counties, following the precedent of the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianlong, the Board of Civil Appointments memorialized requesting imperial selection; the Gaozong emperor ordered ministers, censor-in-chiefs, and vice ministers to recommend fairly from among their department subordinates and from within prefectures and counties, following the precedent of the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 次年，諭「聖祖時如湯斌、陸隴其學問純正，言行相符，陳璸、彭鵬操守清廉，治行卓越。

translations.literal: The following year, an edict stated: "In the time of the Sacred Ancestor, men such as Tang Bin and Lu Longqi had pure and correct learning, with words matching conduct; Chen Bin and Peng Peng had incorruptible conduct and outstanding administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, an edict stated: "In the time of the Sacred Ancestor, men such as Tang Bin and Lu Longqi had pure and correct learning and words that matched their conduct; Chen Bin and Peng Peng had incorruptible conduct and outstanding administrative records.

sentences.zh: 天下之大，人材之眾，豈無與數人頡頏者？

translations.literal: Within the vastness of the empire and the multitude of talent, could there be none to match these several men?
translations.idiomatic: Within the vastness of the empire and the multitude of talent, could there truly be none to match these several men?

sentences.zh: 大學士、九卿其公舉備採擇」。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries and the nine ministers shall jointly recommend candidates for selection."
translations.idiomatic: Let the grand secretaries and the nine ministers jointly recommend candidates for selection."

sentences.zh: 七年，帝思骨鯁質樸之士，如古馬周、陽城起布衣為御史者，詔大學士、九卿及督、撫，勿論資格，列名舉奏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the emperor thought of blunt and plain-spoken men of substance, like the ancients Ma Zhou and Yang Cheng who rose from commoner status to censor; an edict ordered grand secretaries, the nine ministers, and governors-general and governors, regardless of qualifications, to list names and recommend by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the emperor sought blunt and plain-spoken men of substance, like the ancients Ma Zhou and Yang Cheng, who had risen from commoner status to become censors; an edict ordered the grand secretaries, the nine ministers, and the governors-general and governors, regardless of qualifications, to list names and recommend them by memorial.

sentences.zh: 嗣諸臣奏到，下吏部定期考試。

translations.literal: Subsequently, when the officials' memorials arrived, the matter was sent down to the Board of Civil Appointments to schedule examinations on a fixed date.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequently, when the officials' memorials arrived, the matter was sent down to the Board of Civil Appointments to schedule examinations on a fixed date.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，考選御史，試以時務策，帝親取中書胡寶瑔第一。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, censors were selected by examination; they were tested on policy essays concerning current affairs, and the emperor personally ranked the Hanlin bachelor Hu Baochen first.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, censors were selected by examination on policy essays concerning current affairs, and the emperor personally ranked the Hanlin bachelor Hu Baochen first.

sentences.zh: 引見，寶瑔、塗逢震等十人用御史，沈瀾發江南補用。

translations.literal: Upon presentation at court, Hu Baochen, Tu Fengzhen, and nine others were appointed censors; Shen Lan was dispatched to Jiangnan for supplemental appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Upon presentation at court, Hu Baochen, Tu Fengzhen, and nine others were appointed censors; Shen Lan was dispatched to Jiangnan for supplemental appointment.

sentences.zh: 既而從御史李清芳奏，選用御史，令吏部將合例人員奏請考試。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, following censor Li Qingfang's memorial, in selecting and appointing censors the Board of Civil Appointments was ordered to memorialize requesting examination of men meeting the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, following a memorial from the censor Li Qingfang, the selection and appointment of censors was ordered to proceed through the Board of Civil Appointments, which was to memorialize requesting examination of men meeting the regulations.

sentences.zh: 於是保薦御史例罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the precedent of recommending censors was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the practice of recommending censors was abolished.

sentences.zh: 清代未設直言極諫之科，而選擇言官至為慎重，裨益政治，非淺鮮也。

translations.literal: The Qing dynasty did not establish an examination category for blunt remonstrance, yet in selecting remonstrating officials the utmost care was taken; the benefit to governance was no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing dynasty did not establish an examination category for blunt remonstrance, yet the utmost care was taken in selecting remonstrating officials—a benefit to governance that was by no means slight.

sentences.zh: 自康、乾兩朝，敦尚實學，一時名儒碩彥，膺薦擢者，尤難悉數。

translations.literal: From the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, practical learning was earnestly honored; eminent scholars and great worthies of the age who received recommendation and promotion are especially hard to count fully.
translations.idiomatic: From the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, practical learning was earnestly honored; the eminent scholars and great worthies of the age who received recommendation and promotion are especially too numerous to count.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，聖祖問閣臣，在廷中博學能詩文者孰為最？

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, the Sacred Ancestor asked the grand secretaries who among those at court was foremost in broad learning and ability in poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, the Sacred Ancestor asked the grand secretaries who among those at court was foremost in broad learning and ability in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 李霨、馮溥、陳廷敬、張英交口薦戶部郎中王士禎，召對懋勤殿，賦詩稱旨，授翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: Li Wei, Feng Pu, Chen Tingjing, and Zhang Ying unanimously recommended Board of Revenue bureau director Wang Shizhen; summoned for audience at the Hall of Diligent Government, he composed poetry that pleased the emperor and was appointed Hanlin academy reader.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, Feng Pu, Chen Tingjing, and Zhang Ying unanimously recommended the Board of Revenue bureau director Wang Shizhen; summoned for audience at the Hall of Diligent Government, he composed poetry that pleased the emperor and was appointed reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 部曹改詞臣，自士禎始。

translations.literal: A ministry bureau official transferred to literary service—this began with Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: The transfer of a ministry bureau official to literary service began with Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，詔大學士舉長於文學者，王熙、張玉書疏薦在籍尚書徐乾學、左都御史王鴻緒、少詹事高士奇。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, an edict ordered grand secretaries to recommend men accomplished in letters; Wang Xi and Zhang Yushu memorialized recommending the retired minister Xu Qianxue, left censor-in-chief Wang Hongxu, and junior grand tutor Gao Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, an edict ordered the grand secretaries to recommend men accomplished in letters; Wang Xi and Zhang Yushu memorialized recommending the retired minister Xu Qianxue, the left censor-in-chief Wang Hongxu, and the junior grand tutor Gao Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 召來京修書。

translations.literal: They were summoned to the capital to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: They were summoned to the capital to compile books.

sentences.zh: 乾學未聞命卒，詔進呈遺書，並召其弟秉義來京。

translations.literal: Qianxue died before the order reached him; an edict ordered his posthumous writings presented to the throne, and also summoned his younger brother Bingyi to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue died before the order reached him; an edict ordered his posthumous writings presented to the throne and also summoned his younger brother Bingyi to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，大學士李光地薦直隸生員王蘭生入直內廷，尋賜舉人、進士，授編修，洊躋卿貳。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, grand secretary Li Guangdi recommended Zhili licentiate Wang Lansheng to serve in the inner court; soon he was granted juren and jinshi status, appointed compiler, and repeatedly rose to vice ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year, the grand secretary Li Guangdi recommended the Zhili licentiate Wang Lansheng to serve in the inner court; soon he was granted juren and jinshi status, appointed compiler, and repeatedly rose to vice ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 歷康、雍、乾三朝，凡天祿秘書，靡不與校勘之役。

translations.literal: Through the Kangxi, Yongzheng, and Qianlong reigns, of all the imperial library's secret books, none failed to receive his service in collation.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Kangxi, Yongzheng, and Qianlong reigns, he took part in the collation of virtually every work in the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 同時江南何焯，亦以寒儒賜舉人、進士，直南書房，授編修。

translations.literal: At the same time Jiangnan's He Chuo, also as a poor scholar, was granted juren and jinshi status, served in the Southern Library, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time He Chuo of Jiangnan, also a poor scholar, was granted juren and jinshi status, served in the Southern Library, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 被劾解官，仍直書局。

translations.literal: Impeached and dismissed from office, he still served in the book bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached and dismissed from office, he still served in the book bureau.

sentences.zh: 亦光地薦也。

translations.literal: This too was through Guangdi's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: He too had been recommended by Guangdi.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，侍郎兼祭酒孫嘉淦薦舉人雷鋐學行，為國子監學正。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period, vice minister and concurrent chancellor of the National Academy Sun Jiagan recommended juren Lei Hong for learning and conduct, appointing him director of study at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng period, the vice minister and concurrent chancellor of the National Academy Sun Jiagan recommended the juren Lei Hong for learning and conduct and appointed him director of study at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，尚書管監事楊名時薦進士庄亨陽、舉人潘永季、蔡德峻、秦蕙田、吳鼐，貢生官獻瑤、王文震，監生夏宗瀾等，潛心經學，並為國子監屬官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, Minister Yang Mingshi, who also managed academy affairs, recommended jinshi Zhuang Hengyang, juren Pan Yongji, Cai Dejun, Qin Huitian, and Wu Nai, tribute student Guan Xianyao and Wang Wenzhen, and academy student Xia Zonglan and others, all devoted to classical learning, and all were appointed subordinate officials of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianlong, Minister Yang Mingshi, who also managed academy affairs, recommended the jinshi Zhuang Hengyang, the juren Pan Yongji, Cai Dejun, Qin Huitian, and Wu Nai, the tribute students Guan Xianyao and Wang Wenzhen, and the academy student Xia Zonglan and others—all devoted to classical learning—and appointed them subordinate officials of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，詔開四庫館。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, an edict ordered the opening of the Siku Library bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, an edict ordered the opening of the Siku Library bureau.

sentences.zh: 延置儒臣，以翰林官纂輯不敷，大學士劉統勛薦進士邵晉涵、周永年，尚書裘曰修薦進士余集、舉人戴震，尚書王際華薦舉人楊昌霖，同典秘籍。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars were retained; because Hanlin officials alone were insufficient for compilation, grand secretary Liu Tongxun recommended jinshi Shao Jinhan and Zhou Yongnian, Minister Qiu Yuexiu recommended jinshi Yu Ji and juren Dai Zhen, and Minister Wang Jihua recommended juren Yang Changlin; all jointly managed the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars were retained; because Hanlin officials alone were insufficient for compilation, the grand secretary Liu Tongxun recommended the jinshi Shao Jinhan and Zhou Yongnian, Minister Qiu Yuexiu recommended the jinshi Yu Ji and the juren Dai Zhen, and Minister Wang Jihua recommended the juren Yang Changlin—all of whom jointly managed the secret archives.

sentences.zh: 後皆改入翰林，時稱「五徵君」。

translations.literal: Later all were transferred into the Hanlin Academy; at the time they were called "the Five Summoned Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Later all were transferred into the Hanlin Academy; at the time they were called "the Five Summoned Worthies."

sentences.zh: 此其著者也。

translations.literal: These are the notable cases.
translations.idiomatic: These are the most notable cases.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，和珅敗，仁宗下詔求賢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing, when Heshen fell, the Renzong emperor issued an edict seeking the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign, after Heshen's fall, the Renzong emperor issued an edict seeking worthy men.

sentences.zh: 諭滿、漢大臣，密舉操守端潔、才猷幹濟、居官事迹可據者，降敕褎擢廉吏劉清，風厲天下。

translations.literal: An edict directed Manchu and Han ministers secretly to recommend men of upright and incorrupt conduct, capable talent and practical achievement, and verifiable records in office; an imperial rescript was issued honoring and promoting the incorruptible official Liu Qing, to reform morals throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Manchu and Han ministers secretly to recommend men of upright and incorrupt conduct, capable talent, practical achievement, and verifiable records in office; an imperial rescript honoring and promoting the incorruptible official Liu Qing was issued to reform morals throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 十九年，御史卓秉恬請嚴禁濫保，帝是之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, censor Zhuo Bingtian requested strict prohibition of reckless recommendations; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, the censor Zhuo Bingtian requested strict prohibition of reckless recommendations, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，尚書劉鐶之薦起名儒唐鑒，授廣西知府。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong emperor ascended the throne, Minister Liu Huanzhi recommended the renowned scholar Tang Jian and appointed him prefect of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanzong emperor ascended the throne, Minister Liu Huanzhi recommended the renowned scholar Tang Jian and appointed him prefect of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 四川總督蔣攸銛薦川東道陶澍治行第一，擢按察使。

translations.literal: Sichuan governor-general Jiang Yohuan recommended eastern Sichuan circuit intendant Tao Shu as first in administrative achievement and promoted him to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan governor-general Jiang Yohuan recommended the eastern Sichuan circuit intendant Tao Shu as first in administrative achievement and promoted him to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 澍好臧否人物，開籓皖中，入覲論奏，侃侃多所舉劾。

translations.literal: Shu was fond of judging men's merits and faults; when he opened his provincial administration in central Anhui and entered court for audience to discuss and report, he spoke forthrightly and frequently recommended and impeached many men.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was fond of judging men's merits and faults; when he established his provincial administration in central Anhui and came to court to discuss and report affairs, he spoke forthrightly and frequently recommended and impeached many men.

sentences.zh: 宣宗疑之。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong emperor was suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong emperor was suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 密諭巡撫孫爾准察其為人，爾准條列善政，密疏保薦。

translations.literal: A secret edict directed Governor Sun Erzhun to investigate his character; Erzhun itemized his good policies and recommended him in a secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict directed the governor Sun Erzhun to investigate his character; Erzhun itemized his good policies and recommended him in a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 遂獲大用，擢兩江總督。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received great employment and was promoted to governor-general of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he received great employment and was promoted to governor-general of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 臨歿遺疏薦粵督林則徐繼己任。

translations.literal: On the eve of death, in a final memorial he recommended Guangdong governor Lin Zexu to succeed him in office.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his death, in a final memorial he recommended the Guangdong governor Lin Zexu to succeed him in office.

sentences.zh: 澍以知人稱，咸、同中興諸名臣，多為所識拔。

translations.literal: Shu was famed for knowing men; many of the renowned ministers of the Xianfeng and Tongzhi restoration were men he had recognized and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was famed for knowing men; many of the renowned ministers of the Xianfeng and Tongzhi restoration were men he had recognized and promoted.

sentences.zh: 文宗嗣位，詔求直言。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong emperor succeeded to the throne, an edict sought blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wenzong emperor succeeded to the throne, an edict called for blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 侍郎曾國籓疏陳：「本原至計，尤在用人。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zeng Guofan memorialized stating: "The fundamental and utmost plan lies above all in employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zeng Guofan memorialized stating: "The fundamental plan lies above all in employing men.

sentences.zh: 人材有轉移之道，培養之方，考察之法。」

translations.literal: Talent has ways of transfer, methods of cultivation, and means of investigation."
translations.idiomatic: Talent has ways of transfer, methods of cultivation, and means of investigation."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 詔中外大臣薦舉人才。

translations.literal: An edict ordered ministers at court and in the provinces to recommend talent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered ministers at court and in the provinces to recommend talent.

sentences.zh: 大學士穆彰阿奏保宗室文彩，聶澐。

translations.literal: Grand secretary Mujangga memorialized recommending the imperial clansman Wencai and Nie Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretary Mujangga memorialized recommending the imperial clansman Wencai and Nie Yun.

sentences.zh: 特旨用京堂。

translations.literal: A special edict appointed them to capital posts.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict appointed them to capital posts.

sentences.zh: 大學士潘世恩疏薦前總督林則徐、按察使姚瑩、員外郎邵懿辰、中允馮桂芬。

translations.literal: Grand secretary Pan Shi'en memorialized recommending former governor-general Lin Zexu, surveillance commissioner Yao Ying, bureau director Shao Yichen, and palace secretary Feng Guifen.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretary Pan Shi'en memorialized recommending the former governor-general Lin Zexu, the surveillance commissioner Yao Ying, the bureau director Shao Yichen, and the palace secretary Feng Guifen.

sentences.zh: 尚書杜受田首薦則徐及前漕督周天爵。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Du Shoutian first recommended Lin Zexu and former grain transport commissioner Zhou Tianjue.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of works Du Shoutian was the first to recommend Lin Zexu and the former grain transport commissioner Zhou Tianjue.

sentences.zh: 詔起則徐督師，天爵巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Lin Zexu to command troops; Tianjue was made governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Lin Zexu to take command of the armies, and Zhou Tianjue was appointed governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 侍郎曾國籓薦太常少卿李棠階、郎中吳廷棟、通政副使王慶雲、江蘇淮揚道嚴正基、浙江知縣江忠源。

translations.literal: Vice minister Zeng Guofan recommended vice-president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Tangjie, bureau director Wu Tingdong, vice transmission commissioner Wang Qingyun, Jiangsu Huai-Yang intendant Yan Zhengji, and Zhejiang magistrate Jiang Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister Zeng Guofan recommended the vice-president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Tangjie, the bureau director Wu Tingdong, the vice transmission commissioner Wang Qingyun, the Huai-Yang intendant of Jiangsu Yan Zhengji, and the magistrate of Zhejiang Jiang Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 尚書周祖培亦薦棠階、廷棟及郎中易棠等，多蒙擢用。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Zupe also recommended Tangjie, Tingdong, bureau director Yi Tang, and others; many received promotion and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The minister Zhou Zupe likewise recommended Tangjie, Tingdong, the bureau director Yi Tang, and others, many of whom were promoted and appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督吳文鎔、貴州巡撫喬用遷薦知府胡林翼，擢道員。

translations.literal: Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Wu Wenrong and Guizhou governor Qiao Yongqian recommended prefect Hu Linyi; he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou Wu Wenrong and the governor of Guizhou Qiao Yongqian recommended the prefect Hu Linyi, who was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，以各省用兵，詔採訪才兼文武、膽識出眾之士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, because every province was at war, an edict ordered the seeking out of men possessing both civil and military talent, with outstanding courage and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xianfeng reign, with warfare raging across the provinces, an edict commanded that men of combined civil and military ability and exceptional courage and judgment be sought out.

sentences.zh: 御史宗稷辰疏薦湖南左宗棠，浙江姚承輿，江蘇周騰虎、管晏，廣西唐啟華。

translations.literal: Censor Zong Jichen memorialized recommending Hunan's Zuo Zongtang; Zhejiang's Yao Chengyu; Jiangsu's Zhou Tenghu and Guan Yan; and Guangxi's Tang Qihua.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Zong Jichen memorialized recommending Zuo Zongtang of Hunan, Yao Chengyu of Zhejiang, Zhou Tenghu and Guan Yan of Jiangsu, and Tang Qihua of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 命各督、撫訪察，送京引見。

translations.literal: Each governor and governor-general was ordered to investigate, send them to the capital, and present them for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The governors and governor-generals were ordered to investigate these men, send them to the capital, and present them for imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 是時海內多故，粵寇縱橫。

translations.literal: At this time trouble abounded throughout the realm, and Cantonese rebels roamed unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: At that time calamities multiplied across the empire, and the Cantonese rebels ranged unchecked.

sentences.zh: 文慶以大學士直樞廷，屢密請破除滿、漢畛域，用人不拘資地。

translations.literal: Wen Qing, as grand secretary serving at the Grand Council, repeatedly secretly requested the abolition of Manchu-Han boundaries and the use of men without regard to seniority and background.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as grand secretary on the Grand Council, Wen Qing repeatedly urged in private that the barrier between Manchu and Han be dismantled and that appointments should not be bound by rank and pedigree.

sentences.zh: 謂漢人來自田間，知民疾苦，熟諳情偽，辦賊當重用漢人。

translations.literal: He said that Han people came from the fields, knew the people's hardships, were well versed in genuine and false conditions, and that in suppressing bandits Han men ought to be heavily employed.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Han officials, drawn from the countryside, understood the people's sufferings and the realities on the ground, and that Han talent should be heavily relied upon in the suppression of rebels.

sentences.zh: 國籓起鄉兵擊賊，戰失利，謗議紛起。

translations.literal: Guofan raised local militia to attack bandits; battle went badly, and slander and criticism arose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan raised local militia to fight the rebels, but after a defeat criticism and denunciation erupted on all sides.

sentences.zh: 文慶獨謂國籓忠誠負時望，終當建非常功，宜專任討賊。

translations.literal: Wen Qing alone said that Guofan was loyal, bore the hopes of the age, would in the end achieve extraordinary merit, and ought to be solely entrusted with suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing alone maintained that Guofan was loyal and commanded the esteem of the age, that he would eventually achieve extraordinary merit, and that he should be given sole charge of the campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 又嘗奇林翼才略，林翼以貴州道員留楚帶勇剿賊，國籓薦其才堪大用，勝己十倍。

translations.literal: He also once marveled at Lin Yi's talent and stratagem; Lin Yi, as a Guizhou circuit intendant, remained in Hubei leading braves to suppress bandits; Guofan recommended that his talent could serve for great employment, exceeding his own tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: He had also admired Lin Yi's talent and strategic ability. Lin Yi, though a circuit intendant of Guizhou, remained in Hubei at the head of local braves to hunt down rebels, and Guofan recommended him as a man of talents far surpassing his own—ten times his equal.

sentences.zh: 一歲間擢湖北巡撫，文慶實中主之。

translations.literal: Within one year he was promoted to Hubei governor; Wen Qing had in truth been the central supporter.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Lin Yi was promoted to governor of Hubei, with Wen Qing serving as the principal patron behind the appointment.

sentences.zh: 袁甲三督師淮上，駱秉章巡撫湖南，文慶薦其才，請勿他調，以觀厥成。

translations.literal: Yuan Jiasan commanded troops on the Huai; Luo Bingzhang governed Hunan; Wen Qing recommended their talents and requested that they not be transferred elsewhere, to observe their completion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiasan was commanding on the Huai River front and Luo Bingzhang was governing Hunan. Wen Qing praised their abilities and urged that they not be transferred elsewhere, so that their achievements might be allowed to ripen.

sentences.zh: 時論稱之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion widely approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，林翼奏興國處士萬斛泉及其弟子宋鼎、鄒金粟，砥礪廉隅，不求仕進，請予獎勵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Lin Yi memorialized that Xingguo scholar-unaffiliated Wan Huquan and his disciples Song Ding and Zou Jinli, who had cultivated integrity and sought no advancement, should be granted reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Lin Yi memorialized on behalf of the recluse Wan Huquan of Xingguo and his disciples Song Ding and Zou Jinli, men of scrupulous integrity who sought no official advancement, requesting that they be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 詔賞斛泉等七品冠服有差。

translations.literal: An edict awarded Huquan and the others seventh-rank caps and robes with distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict conferred caps and robes of seventh rank upon Huquan and the others, with distinctions according to merit.

sentences.zh: 時軍事方殷，迭飭疆吏及各路統兵大臣奏舉將才。

translations.literal: At that time military affairs were pressing; repeatedly frontier officials and commanding generals on every route were ordered to memorialize recommending generals' talents.
translations.idiomatic: With military affairs then at their height, frontier officials and commanding generals on every front were repeatedly ordered to memorial recommending men of military talent.

sentences.zh: 林翼舉左宗棠，予四品京堂，襄辦國籓軍務。

translations.literal: Lin Yi recommended Zuo Zongtang; he was given fourth-rank Beijing official rank and assisted in managing Guofan's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi recommended Zuo Zongtang, who was given fourth-rank Beijing official status and appointed to assist in managing Guofan's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨、劉蓉、張運蘭，命國籓、林翼調遣。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen, Liu Rong, and Zhang Yunlan were ordered to be deployed by Guofan and Lin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen, Liu Rong, and Zhang Yunlan were placed under the dispatch of Guofan and Lin Yi.

sentences.zh: 他如塔齊布、羅澤南、李續賓、李續宜、彭玉麟、楊岳斌等，俱以末弁或諸生，拔自戎行，聲績爛然。

translations.literal: Others such as Ta Qibu, Luo Zinan, Li Xubin, Li Xuyi, Peng Yulin, and Yang Yuebin—all, as low-ranking officers or licentiates, plucked from the ranks of war—won resplendent reputations and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Others such as Ta Qibu, Luo Zinan, Li Xubin, Li Xuyi, Peng Yulin, and Yang Yuebin—all low-ranking officers or mere licentiates plucked from the battle lines—won resounding fame for their achievements.

sentences.zh: 曾、胡知人善任，薦賢滿天下，卒奏中興之功。

translations.literal: Zeng and Hu knew men and employed them well, recommended the worthy throughout the realm, and in the end achieved the merit of national revival.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng and Hu knew how to recognize talent and put it to use, recommending worthy men across the empire until at last the work of national revival was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 穆宗踐阼，以軍興後吏治廢弛，特擢天津知府石贊清為順天府尹，諭各省訪察循良，有伏處山林、德行醇備、學問淵通之士，督、撫、學政據實奏聞。

translations.literal: The Muzong Emperor ascended the throne; because after the military rise administration had fallen into laxity, he specially promoted Tianjin prefect Shi Zanqing to Shuntian metropolitan magistrate, instructing every province to seek out conscientious administrators, and scholars dwelling hidden in mountains and forests, of pure virtue and profound learning—governors, governors-general, and education commissioners to memorialize truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne, he found that administration had grown lax in the wake of prolonged warfare. He specially promoted the prefect of Tianjin, Shi Zanqing, to metropolitan magistrate of Shuntian, and instructed the provinces to seek out conscientious administrators, as well as scholars of pure virtue and profound learning dwelling in seclusion—governors, governor-generals, and education commissioners were to report on such men according to fact.

sentences.zh: 尋國籓疏稱常州士民尚節義，城陷與賊相持。

translations.literal: Soon Guofan memorialized that Changzhou scholar-gentry and commoners honored integrity and righteousness; when the city fell they resisted the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guofan memorialized that the people of Changzhou held fast to integrity and righteousness, continuing to resist the rebels even after the city had fallen.

sentences.zh: 其士子多讀書稽古。

translations.literal: Their scholar-youth mostly read books and examined antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Many of their men of letters were steeped in classical learning and historical study.

sentences.zh: 如候選同知劉翰清，監生趙烈文、方駿謨、華蘅芳，從九品徐壽等，若使閱歷戎行，廓其聞見，有裨軍謀。

translations.literal: Such as expectant sub-prefect Liu Hanqing, students Zhao Liewen, Fang Junmo, and Hua Hengfang, ninth-rank clerk Xu Shou, and others—if they were made to experience military service and broaden their knowledge and observation, it would benefit military planning.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were the expectant sub-prefect Liu Hanqing, the students Zhao Liewen, Fang Junmo, and Hua Hengfang, and the ninth-rank clerk Xu Shou. If given experience on campaign to broaden their horizons, they would prove valuable to military planning.

sentences.zh: 詔譚廷襄、嚴樹森、左宗棠、薛煥訪求，遣送國籓軍營錄用。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tan Tingxiang, Yan Shusen, Zuo Zongtang, and Xue Huan to seek them out and send them to Guofan's military camp for employment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded Tan Tingxiang, Yan Shusen, Zuo Zongtang, and Xue Huan to seek out these men and forward them to Guofan's camp for appointment.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，諭廷臣曰：「上年屢降旨令保舉人才，各督、撫已將政績卓著人員登諸薦牘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, the emperor instructed the court officials, saying: 'Last year edicts were repeatedly issued ordering the recommendation of talent; each governor and governor-general has already entered persons of outstanding administrative achievement on recommendation memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign, the emperor addressed the court: 'Last year I repeatedly issued edicts calling for the recommendation of talented men, and the governors and governor-generals have already entered men of outstanding achievement on their recommendation lists.

sentences.zh: 在京如大學士周祖培，大學士銜祁■A4藻、翁心存，協辦大學士倭仁，侍郎宋晉、王茂廕，科道高延祜、薛春藜、郭祥瑞等，各有薦舉。

translations.literal: In the capital, such as grand secretary Zhou Zupe, grand secretary-rank Qi Zhizao and Weng Xincun, assistant grand secretary Woren, vice ministers Song Jin and Wang Maoyin, and censorial officials Gao Yanhu, Xue Chunli, Guo Xiangrui, and others—each had recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, the grand secretary Zhou Zupe, Qi Zhizao and Weng Xincun with grand secretary rank, the assistant grand secretary Woren, the vice ministers Song Jin and Wang Maoyin, and the censorial officials Gao Yanhu, Xue Chunli, and Guo Xiangrui, among others—each submitted recommendations of their own.

sentences.zh: 人臣以人事君，不必俟有明詔，始可敷陳。

translations.literal: Ministers serve the ruler through recommending men; they need not wait for an explicit edict before they may set forth recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers serve their sovereign through the recommendation of men; they need not wait for an explicit edict before presenting their views.

sentences.zh: 其各臚列事實，秉公保奏。」

translations.literal: Let each exhaustively list facts and impartially recommend and memorialize.'
translations.idiomatic: Let each set forth the facts in full and recommend candidates with impartiality.

sentences.zh: 復屢諭國籓保薦督撫大員。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly also instructed Guofan to recommend and nominate great provincial officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also repeatedly instructed Guofan to recommend high provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 國籓言：「封疆將帥，惟天子舉措之。

translations.literal: Guofan said: 'Frontier generals and marshals are for the Son of Heaven alone to appoint and dismiss.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan replied: 'Governors-general and military commanders are for the Son of Heaven alone to appoint and remove.

sentences.zh: 四方多故，疆臣既有征伐之權，不當更分黜陟之柄，宜防外重內輕之漸，兼杜植私樹黨之端。」

translations.literal: The four quarters have many troubles; frontier officials already have the authority of campaign and conquest—they ought not further to share the power of promotion and demotion; one should guard against the tendency of outer strength and inner weakness, and also block the openings for cultivating private factions.
translations.idiomatic: With trouble on every front, frontier officials already wield the power of war—they should not also share authority over promotions and dismissals. We must guard against the provinces growing stronger than the center, and forestall the rise of private patronage and factionalism.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒答。

translations.literal: The emperor responded with an edict of gracious praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with an edict of gracious commendation.

sentences.zh: 二年，河南學政景其濬奏副貢生蘇源生等學行，授本省訓導。

translations.literal: In the second year, Henan education commissioner Jing Qijun memorialized on the learning and conduct of vice tribute student Su Yuansheng and others; they were appointed instructors in the province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the education commissioner of Henan, Jing Qijun, memorialized on the scholarship and conduct of the vice tribute graduate Su Yuansheng and others, who were appointed instructors within the province.

sentences.zh: 命各學臣訪舉經明行修之士，酌保數人，不為恆制。

translations.literal: Each education commissioner was ordered to seek and recommend men of mastery in the classics and cultivation in conduct, recommending several men as appropriate—not as a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Education commissioners throughout the empire were ordered to seek out men of classical learning and upright conduct and recommend a suitable number—not as a standing rule, but as occasion warranted.

sentences.zh: 九年，浙江學政徐樹銘，以採訪儒修，疏薦已革編修俞樾，請賞還原銜，送部引見；

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Zhejiang education commissioner Xu Shuming, in seeking Confucian scholars, memorialized recommending dismissed compiler Yu Yue, requesting restoration of his original rank and transmission to the ministry for audience;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the education commissioner of Zhejiang, Xu Shuming, while seeking out learned Confucians, memorialized recommending the dismissed compiler Yu Yue, asking that his original rank be restored and that he be sent to the ministry for audience;

sentences.zh: 秀水教諭譚廷獻、舉人趙銘、江西拔貢楊希閔等，比照召試博學鴻詞例，予廷試。

translations.literal: Xiushui instructor Tan Tingxian, provincial graduate Zhao Ming, Jiangxi selected tribute graduate Yang Ximin, and others—by analogy to the summons and examination for erudition and literary excellence—were granted palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: The instructor of Xiushui Tan Tingxian, the provincial graduate Zhao Ming, the selected tribute graduate of Jiangxi Yang Ximin, and others were, following the precedent of the special examination for erudition and literary excellence, granted a palace examination.

sentences.zh: 帝以樹銘私心自用，下部嚴議，鐫四級。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shuming acted from private motives on his own authority, sent the matter down for severe deliberation and reduced him four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deemed Shuming guilty of acting from private motive on his own authority; the case was referred for severe deliberation, and he was demoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 此因薦舉獲譴，乃其變也。

translations.literal: This punishment received through recommendation was thus a departure from the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus did a recommendation lead to punishment—a departure from the usual course.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，兩廣督臣張樹聲、撫臣裕寬，薦在籍紳士山西襄陵知縣南海進士硃次琦，國子監典籍銜番禺舉人陳澧篤行。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, the two Guang governors Zhang Shusheng and governor Yu Kuan recommended home-dwelling gentry: former Xiangling magistrate of Shanxi, Nanhai jinshi Zhu Ciqi, and Guozijian lexicographer-rank Panyu provincial graduate Chen Li, for upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Guangxu reign, the governor-general and governor of the two Guang provinces, Zhang Shusheng and Yu Kuan, recommended two home-dwelling scholars of eminent character: Zhu Ciqi of Nanhai, a jinshi and former magistrate of Xiangling in Shanxi, and Chen Li of Panyu, a provincial graduate holding lexicographer rank at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 詔予五品卿銜，以勵績學。

translations.literal: An edict granted fifth-rank honorary chamberlain rank, to encourage profound scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: An edict conferred honorary fifth-rank chamberlain titles upon them, to encourage men of profound scholarship.

sentences.zh: 十年，以外釁迭啟，時事日艱。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, because foreign troubles opened one after another, affairs of the day grew daily harder.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, as foreign crises erupted in succession, the situation grew daily more desperate.

sentences.zh: 諭大學士、六部、九卿、直省將軍、督、撫：「無論文武兩途，有體用賅備，謀勇俱優，或諳習吏治兵事，熟悉中外交涉，或善制船械，精通算術，或饒有機智，饒勇善戰，或諳諫水師及沿海情形者，廣為訪求，具實陳奏。」

translations.literal: An edict to grand secretaries, the six ministries, nine chief courts, and governors and generals of direct provinces: 'Whether of civil or military track, those possessing combined substance and utility, superior in both strategy and courage, or skilled in administration and military affairs and familiar with Sino-foreign dealings, or adept at building ships and armaments and proficient in mathematics, or richly endowed with ingenuity, richly brave and skilled in battle, or versed in foreign navies and coastal conditions—widely seek them out and truthfully memorialize.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict addressed to the grand secretaries, the six ministries, the nine chief courts, and the governors and generals of the provinces: 'Whether civil or military, seek out widely those who unite breadth of learning with practical ability, who excel in counsel and courage alike, who are versed in administration and military affairs and familiar with dealings between China and foreign powers, who are skilled in shipbuilding and armaments and masterful in mathematics, who possess ingenuity and boldness in equal measure, or who understand foreign navies and coastal conditions. Report on such men truthfully in memorial.'

sentences.zh: 二十一年，訪求奇才異能，精天文、地輿、算法、格致、製造學者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, extraordinary talents and unusual abilities were sought—scholars proficient in astronomy, geography, mathematics, natural science, and manufacturing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, the court sought out men of extraordinary talent and rare ability—scholars skilled in astronomy, geography, mathematics, natural science, and engineering.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，翰林院侍讀學士徐致靖疏薦工部主事康有為、刑部主事張元濟、湖南鹽法長寶道黃遵憲、江蘇知府譚嗣同、廣東舉人梁啟超，特予召見。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Hanlin Academy reader Xu Zhijing memorialized recommending Works bureau director Kang Youwei, Punishments bureau director Zhang Yuanji, Hunan salt controller Huang Zunxian, Jiangsu prefect Tan Sitong, and Guangdong provincial graduate Liang Qichao; they were specially summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, the Hanlin reader Xu Zhijing memorialized recommending Kang Youwei, director in the Ministry of Works; Zhang Yuanji, director in the Ministry of Punishments; Huang Zunxian, salt controller of Hunan; Tan Sitong, prefect of Jiangsu; and Liang Qichao, provincial graduate of Guangdong. All were specially summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 徵遵憲、嗣同至京，賞啟超六品銜，任譯書局事。

translations.literal: Huang Zunxian and Tan Sitong were summoned to the capital; Liang Qichao was granted sixth-rank rank and entrusted with the Translation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zunxian and Tan Sitong were summoned to the capital. Liang Qichao was granted sixth-rank status and put in charge of the Translation Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時德宗親政，激於外勢，亟圖自彊。

translations.literal: At that time the Dezong Emperor personally held power, stirred by foreign pressure, urgently sought self-strengthening.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxu Emperor had then assumed personal rule. Stirred by foreign pressure, he urgently pursued policies of self-strengthening.

sentences.zh: 詔求通達時務人才，中外紛紛薦舉。

translations.literal: An edict sought men of talent who comprehended affairs of the age; within and without, recommendations poured in.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts called for men of talent versed in affairs of the day, and recommendations poured in from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 而草茅新進之臣，刻勵求新，昌言變法矣。

translations.literal: Meanwhile newly risen ministers from the grass roots, striving after innovation, openly advocated reform.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile a new generation of officials risen from humble ranks, burning with zeal for innovation, openly championed reform.

sentences.zh: 未幾黨禍起，慈禧皇太后訓政，有為竄海外，其弟廣仁及御史楊深秀、軍機章京譚嗣同、林旭、楊銳、劉光第棄市，致靖以黨附下獄禁錮，復追論原保諸臣罪。

translations.literal: Before long the factional disaster erupted; Empress Dowager Cixi assumed regency; Kang Youwei fled overseas; his younger brother Kang Guangren and censor Yang Shenxiu, Grand Council clerks Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, Yang Rui, and Liu Guangdi were executed in the marketplace; Xu Zhijing was imprisoned for factional affiliation; and the original recommending officials were pursued for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the purge of the reform faction began. Empress Dowager Cixi resumed regency. Kang Youwei fled abroad. His younger brother Kang Guangren, the censor Yang Shenxiu, and the Grand Council clerks Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, Yang Rui, and Liu Guangdi were executed in the marketplace. Xu Zhijing was imprisoned for his factional ties, and those who had originally recommended the reformers were prosecuted in turn.

sentences.zh: 御史宋伯魯、湖南巡撫陳寶箴，開缺戶部尚書、協辦大學士翁同龢，俱削官永不敘用。

translations.literal: Censor Song Bolu, Hunan governor Chen Baozhen, and discharged minister of revenue and assistant grand secretary Weng Tonghe were all stripped of office and permanently barred from appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Song Bolu, the governor of Hunan Chen Baozhen, and the discharged minister of revenue and assistant grand secretary Weng Tonghe were all stripped of office and permanently barred from further appointment.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李端棻謫戍邊，內閣學士張百熙下部議處。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Li Duanfen was banished in penal servitude to the frontier; grand secretary Zhang Baixi was sent down for deliberation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of rites Li Duanfen was banished to penal servitude on the frontier, and the grand secretary Zhang Baixi was referred for deliberation and punishment.

sentences.zh: 其他言新政者，斥逐殆盡。

translations.literal: Others who spoke of the new policies were driven out, almost to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly every voice still advocating the new policies was driven from office.

sentences.zh: 迨庚子京師遘亂，越年和議成，兩宮西幸迴鑾，時事日棘。

translations.literal: When in the Gengzi year disorder struck the capital, the next year peace was concluded, the two palaces returned from their western progress, and affairs of the day grew daily more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Gengzi upheaval in the capital, peace was negotiated the following year and the two empresses returned from their flight west—but the situation grew more urgent by the day.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，詔中外大臣訪求人才，不拘官階大小，有無官職，確知才堪大用，及擅專長者，切實薦舉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, an edict ordered Chinese and foreign great officials to seek talent without regard to rank high or low, with or without office—those known with certainty to be capable of great employment, or possessing specialized excellence—to recommend truly and substantively.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year, an edict commanded officials throughout the empire to seek out talent without regard to rank or official status—men known to be capable of great service, or men of proven specialized skill—and to recommend them with concrete substantiation.

sentences.zh: 派王大臣察驗詢問，出具考語，召見。

translations.literal: Princely great ministers were dispatched to examine, inquire, issue evaluation statements, and summon for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and senior ministers were dispatched to examine and question the candidates, submit evaluations, and present them for audience.

sentences.zh: 於時被薦人員，分起赴京，除官錄用者，至宣統間猶未已。

translations.literal: At that time recommended personnel set out in groups for the capital; those appointed and employed in office continued even into the Xuantong period without cessation.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended men set out for the capital in successive groups; appointments continued to be made from their ranks even into the Xuantong reign.

sentences.zh: 然自光緒之季，改訂官制，增衙署，置官缺，破格錄用人員輒以千數，薦擢亦太濫矣。

translations.literal: Yet from the late Guangxu period, as the official system was revised, yamens increased, official posts were created, and personnel appointed outside normal channels ran to thousands—the recommendations and promotions had grown far too lax.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the late Guangxu period onward, as the bureaucracy was reorganized, new offices multiplied and new posts were created. Extraordinary appointments ran into the thousands, and recommendations and promotions had grown recklessly permissive.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，御史謝遠涵言：「變法至今，長官但舉故舊，士夫不諱鑽營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, censor Xie Yuanhan said: 'From reform until now, chief officials recommend only old associates; scholar-officials do not scruple at currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuantong reign, the censor Xie Yuanhan memorialized: 'Since the reforms began, chief officials have recommended only their old associates, and men of letters no longer shrink from currying favor.

sentences.zh: 請嚴定章程，以貪劣聞者，反坐薦主，加以懲處。」

translations.literal: I request that regulations be strictly fixed: those known for greed and inferiority—their recommending patrons should be punished in turn and subjected to penalty.'
translations.idiomatic: I request that strict regulations be established so that when a recommended man proves corrupt or incompetent, his patron shall be held accountable and punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 疏下所司而已。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office—and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the responsible office—and nothing more was done.

sentences.zh: 薦舉不拘流品。

translations.literal: Recommendations were not bound by social category.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations were not confined to any single social category.

sentences.zh: 清代才臣，以佐雜洊躋開府者，如雍正間之李衛、田文鏡，乾隆間之楊景素、李世傑，政績最著。

translations.literal: Qing talented ministers who from assistant and miscellaneous ranks successively rose to grand governor status, such as Yongzheng-era Li Wei and Tian Wenjing, Qianlong-era Yang Jingsu and Li Shijie—their administrative achievements were most notable.
translations.idiomatic: Among Qing officials of talent who rose from lowly assistant ranks to provincial governorships, none achieved more renown than Li Wei and Tian Wenjing in the Yongzheng reign, and Yang Jingsu and Li Shijie in the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 厥後捐納日廣，起家雜流，膺顯擢者無算，其人大都饒有幹局，以視科目循資遷轉，以資格坐致高位，蓋不侔也。

translations.literal: Thereafter purchase of office daily expanded; men starting from miscellaneous ranks who received conspicuous promotion were beyond counting; such men for the most part possessed abundant practical capacity—compared with examination-route officials advancing by seniority and attaining high position by qualification alone, they were indeed not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, as the purchase of office grew ever more common, countless men of miscellaneous origins won prominent promotion. Most among them possessed genuine administrative capacity—quite unlike examination graduates who ascended by seniority alone and attained high office through qualification rather than merit.

sentences.zh: 薦舉之尤異者，康熙初，陝西提督王進寶，薦其子用予材武可勝副將，後以功擢總兵，父子同建節鉞。

translations.literal: Among the most unusual recommendations: in early Kangxi, Shaanxi provincial commander Wang Jinbao recommended his son Wang Yong for martial ability sufficient for deputy commander; later by merit he was promoted to commander-in-chief—father and son together established military seals of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Among the most unusual cases of recommendation: in early Kangxi, the provincial commander of Shaanxi Wang Jinbao recommended his own son Wang Yong as a man of martial ability fit for deputy commander. Wang Yong was later promoted to commander-in-chief by merit, and father and son alike came to bear the seals of military authority.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，雲南總兵趙坤擢貴州提督，請以其子秉鐸為貴州提標參將，帝允所請。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period, Yunnan regional commander Zhao Kun was promoted to Guizhou provincial commander; he requested his son Bingduo as Guizhou provincial garrison deputy commander; the emperor granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign, the regional commander of Yunnan Zhao Kun was promoted to provincial commander of Guizhou and requested that his son Bingduo be appointed deputy commander of the Guizhou garrison. The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 孫嘉淦為祭酒，舉其弟揚淦為國子監學正，湖南衡永郴桂道汪榯，且薦其父原任刑部司官澐學問優裕，政事練達，授四川知府。

translations.literal: Sun Jiagan as chancellor of the Imperial Academy recommended his younger brother Yanggan as Guozijian director of studies; Hunan Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit intendant Wang Qi moreover recommended his father, former Punishments ministry clerk Yun, for ample learning and practiced administration—appointed Sichuan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiagan, chancellor of the Imperial Academy, recommended his younger brother Yanggan as a director of studies at the Guozijian. Wang Qi, intendant of the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui circuit in Hunan, went further and recommended his own father Yun, a former clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, as a man of ample learning and seasoned administration; Yun was appointed prefect of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 此則舉不避親，其破除成例又如此。

translations.literal: Here recommendation did not avoid kin; breaking established precedents went thus far.
translations.idiomatic: In such cases recommendation did not shrink from nepotism—and the breaking of precedent could go just as far.

sentences.zh: 徵辟幕僚，雍正元年詔吏部，嗣後督撫所延幕賓，將姓名具奏，稱職者題部議敘，授之職位，以示砥礪。

translations.literal: Regarding recruitment of staff: in the first year of Yongzheng an edict to the Ministry of Personnel said that hereafter staff retained by governors and governor-generals should have names fully memorialized; those who performed their duties would be referred to the ministry for deliberation on promotion and granted office, to show encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: As for the recruitment of private secretaries: in the first year of the Yongzheng reign, an edict to the Ministry of Personnel directed that henceforth governors and governor-generals were to memorialize the names of their retained staff; those who performed competently would be referred to the ministry for promotion and granted official posts, as a measure of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，侍郎吳應棻以鼓勵賢才，請立勸懲之法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, vice minister Wu Yingfen, to encourage worthy talent, requested establishment of laws of reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, the vice minister Wu Yingfen petitioned for the establishment of a system of rewards and punishments to encourage worthy talent.

sentences.zh: 洎道光間，幕友濫邀甄敘，台諫屢以為言，詔督、撫、鹽政，一切議敘，不許保列幕友，並嚴禁本省屬員濫充，違者吏部查參議處。

translations.literal: Down to the Daoguang period, staff indiscriminately sought deliberation on promotion; censorial officials repeatedly spoke of it; an edict to governors, governor-generals, and salt controllers—for all deliberation on promotion, staff were not permitted to be recommended; local subordinates acting as staff without authorization were strictly forbidden; violators would be investigated and punished by the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: By the Daoguang reign, private secretaries were routinely petitioning for formal promotion, a practice repeatedly decried by the censoriate. An edict directed governors, governor-generals, and salt controllers that staff were no longer to be included in promotion deliberations, and that the unauthorized appointment of local subordinates as private secretaries was strictly forbidden; violators were to be investigated and punished by the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 然康熙時，布衣陳潢佐靳輔治河，特賜僉事道銜。

translations.literal: Yet in Kangxi times, commoner Chen Huang assisting Jin Fu in river control was specially granted vice intendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Kangxi reign, the commoner Chen Huang, who assisted Jin Fu in river conservancy, was specially granted the rank of vice intendant.

sentences.zh: 雍正時，方觀承為定邊大將軍平郡王記室，以布衣召見，賜中書銜。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng times, Fang Guancheng as secretary to the Pacifying Prince, general of frontier pacification, was summoned as a commoner for audience and granted secretariat rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign, Fang Guancheng, secretary to the Pacifying Prince, frontier-pacifying general, was summoned to audience as a commoner and granted the rank of secretariat compiler.

sentences.zh: 乾、嘉間，名臣如王傑、嚴如煜、林則徐輩，皆先佐幕而後通籍。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong and Jiaqing periods, noted ministers such as Wang Jie, Yan Ruyu, Lin Zexu, and their like—all first served on staffs and afterward entered the registers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns, eminent officials such as Wang Jie, Yan Ruyu, and Lin Zexu all first served as private secretaries before entering official ranks.

sentences.zh: 迨咸、同軍興，左宗棠、李鴻章、劉蓉等，多以幕僚佐績戎旃，成中興之業。

translations.literal: When in the Xianfeng and Tongzhi military rise, Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, Liu Rong, and others—mostly as staff—assisted in military banners and achieved the work of national revival.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare erupted in the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, Liu Rong, and others rose largely through staff service, assisting at the battlefront and helping to accomplish the work of national revival.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓總制軍務，幕府號多才，賓從極一時人選，尤卓卓可紀者也。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan's overall command of military affairs—his staff was famed for abundant talent; his retainers represented the finest men of the age; this above all is outstanding and worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zeng Guofan's overall command of military affairs, his staff became legendary for its abundance of talent—his retainers counted among the finest men of the age, a fact above all worthy of record.
